content: “真理使你自由” 柴静Chai Jing Chai’s Substack  Nov 14, 2026 毛泽东想留下胡适，胡适问：“他们要我吗？” 1948年冬天，内战向北平逼近，蒋介石和毛泽东都在留胡适。胡适是北京大学的校长，当时中国最有影响力的知识分子之一。 南京的国民政府送来了三张机票：给胡适、他的妻子，和他儿子胡思杜。 在北大的校长办公室，有人传来了消息，说解放区的广播劝胡适留下，继续做北京大学的校长，兼北京图书馆馆长。这是毛泽东的意思。一年前，他在陕北提到了胡适，说将来进城之后，可以让他当图书馆的馆长。 30年前，毛泽东本人在北大图书馆做助理员。后来他对斯诺说过，那个时候他十分钦佩胡适和陈独秀的文章。 解放区的广播传到校长办公室的时候，季羡林在场。他说，大家都在看胡适的反应。胡适微微一笑，说： “他们要我吗？” 战争已经打到华北，他还在北平的广播当中劝国共双方：容许反对党，国家通过法定的和平方式转移政权，使人民有选择的机会。这是胡适多年的主张。 胡适录音：自由表达和公开反对，是使人民的抱怨、抗议和不满得以表达、被人听见的安全阀。 江冬秀的侄子江丕桓说，胡适的观点在当时的北大学生中已经基本没有市场。胡适问过他，要不要一起离开北平。他回答说：“你们走你们的路，我们走我们的路，我们不走。” 胡适在广播中说过，他很清楚年轻人要的是暴力革命，不是和平演进。但他说，近代以来的历史已经说明，彻底革命的结果会是绝对专制，因为它不能容忍异己，不容许思想和言论的自由。 他自己相信的是实验主义，也就是只承认一点一滴做到的、经过检验的进步。这是他的老师、美国哲学家杜威的思想。 他给儿子起名叫胡思杜，“杜”，就是杜威。 杜威：……他们从人生中学习，而不只是书中。 父亲给儿子取名字，有纪念，也有期许。但是儿子有他自己喜欢的作家。胡家从来宾客如云，胡思杜只给一个人挂过大衣，那个人就是鲁迅。 胡思杜整理的他父亲藏书当中，有一本马克思主义著作，这是他的堂兄留下的。胡家的年轻人当中，地下党员不止一位，其中一人叫石原皋。他说胡思杜追求进步，执意留下。 1948年12月13日夜里，北平西郊响起了炮声。胡适在给辅仁大学的校长陈垣写信，谈到《水经注》的考证。这封信被电话打断了6次。 胡适跟陈垣两个人都在南京抢救学人计划的名单上，但是陈垣没走。 【党史视频：地下党派专人拜访陈垣，一番面谈后，陈垣决心留下。当胡适来邀请陈垣同机南下时，他坚决地拒绝了，后来解释说：“因无走之必要也。”】 朱光潜、沈从文也都在名单上，他们没有走。就像这位北大的武兆发教授一样，他们的家小、学生、学校都在北平。中研院81位院士，留下的是多数。胡适的秘书邓广铭也回忆，思杜是自愿不走的。他说：“我又没有做什么有害共产党的事，他们不会把我怎么样。” 邓广铭推测说，胡适没有勉强自己的儿子一起走，一部分原因也是因为南下之后命运未卜。因为12月14日飞机来接人的时候，都无法降落，当时的南苑机场已经在炮火之下。直到深夜，傅作义打电话通知胡适，让他明早8点走。胡适连夜清点三大柜《水经注》，叮嘱儿子：借来的怎么归还，留下的怎么处置。 这是他们父子在一起的最后一夜，两个人都没有睡。 第二天黎明，胡适夫妇离开家。江冬秀舍不得儿子，又没有办法，给他留了一箱细软和首饰，将来结婚用。 胡适到南京的当晚，在日记里写：儿子思杜留在北平，没有同行。 那一晚，北平完全被困，停电停水。政府要求居民在门口挂起红灯笼，但是在西北风中，没有几盏灯能够保持不灭。 两天之后，12月17日，是北京大学50周年校庆，也是胡适父子共同的生日。胡适在南京回顾北大50年来的战乱流离，祝福它长寿康强。他自称“不名誉的逃兵”，哽咽得说不下去。 这一天的北大，除了有学生在民主广场挖避弹的战壕，一片死寂。 毛泽东点了他的名，胡适说：我的老朋友没有不说话的自由了 将近一个月之后，1949年1月7日，胡思杜给父母写信，说到父亲留下的书装了98箱，已经存进了北大。 胡适日后对朋友说过，是因为思杜自愿留下替他打包书，书存进北大之后，人已经出不来了。但是一直到胡思杜写这封信两个月之后，仍然有北大学生陆续到达上海。胡思杜的信中，并没有寻找机会去会合父母的意思。他说他已经调入了北大图书馆，“一切都好，请勿念”。 同一时间，已经加入地下党的那位亲戚石原皋，还在设法留下胡适。他劝江冬秀回安徽老家，说：“你和儿子都在，胡适一定会回来。”江冬秀被说动了，胡适没有。他在1月把妻子送上了去台湾的船。 3月25日，毛泽东进入北平。10天之后，胡适从上海乘船去美国。 4月21日，他的船到旧金山的时候，记者带着报纸登船，胡适才看到：和谈已经破裂，长江失守。而新华社的标题，对他是尖锐的讽刺。 胡适回忆，1949这一年，他极度苦闷，抬不起头，说不出话。 这个春天，胡思杜搬进了中老胡同的北大宿舍，成为了沈从文的邻居。沈从文只有小学学历，是胡适请他当了大学老师。 胡适（录音）：我们希望两个标准，一个呢，是人的文学，要有人味，要有点人气，要有点人格，要有点人味，人的文学。第二，我们提倡，我们希望要一个自由的文学。文学这些东西不能够由政府来辅导，更不能够由政府来指导。 胡适走后不久，沈从文就失去了北大国文系的位置。他在学校看到了郭沫若斥责他“反动文艺”的大字报，而且收到了匿名的恐吓信。他身心崩溃，试图结束生命。 沈从文11岁的小儿子说，父亲出事之后，家中渐渐少有来客。新搬来的邻居也不跟人交往，只是站在门口活动腿脚，旁边站着一只乌黑发亮的长毛波斯猫。 胡家的黑猫很有名，它进过胡适的诗、徐悲鸿的画和凌叔华的小说。别人叫不动，总是守在自己的门口晒太阳。 沈虎雏叫这位邻居“胡三爷”。胡三爷白白胖胖，穿一件中式上衣，总是笑嘻嘻的。他请小男孩到家里说话，给他看一个比饺子还小的金元宝，给他闻青花瓷坛里面泡的枣子酒，说：“我就是喜欢喝两口。” 像是在承认一个弱点。 胡思杜爱吃喝，爱京戏，有时候也爱赌。母亲骂他：“死没出息。”罗尔纲是他的童年老师，说胡思杜能够唱郝寿臣的一口好戏，如果不是生在这样的家庭，也许能够给舞台增加光彩。可是他是胡适的儿子。 其实胡适18岁的时候也喝酒赌博，请人教唱戏。日后他曾经写信跟妻子说，不要老骂孩子。他惭愧他平时不跟他们亲热，只晓得责怪他们功课不好、习气不好。 胡思杜日后批判他父亲的时候也带着敬畏，说他是“清高纯洁的好人”。 有一天，胡思杜笑着问11岁的沈虎雏：“小弟，你知道吗？毛泽东领导了五四运动。”两个人相视而笑。 11岁的小男孩读过书，知道胡三爷的父亲是五四时代的领袖之一。 但在胡适看来，五四的领导人既不是他本人，也不是毛泽东，这是一场学生自发的爱国运动。 胡适：但这个胜利有两个严重后果…在公众眼中，大学里的思想运动迅速变成了各政党的新武器。在我看来，这是一个十分不幸的后果。 1949年5月，周恩来在北大和教授们座谈，批评胡适没有否定旧制度的勇气，说他“骨头是软的”。 此时胡思杜还在北大。他说，听到周恩来说胡适“根本不认识什么是帝国主义”，他心中反感已极，认为以他父亲的渊博，竟不知什么是帝国主义，宁非侮辱。 胡适：我们坦率承认，中国的许多弊病，大部分来自我们自己的错误和弱点。我们不把责任全归咎于帝国主义或帝国主义的侵略。 周恩来讲话两天之后，《人民日报》登出了辅仁大学校长陈垣给胡适的公开信，说：“你曾经告诉我，共产党之下绝无自由吗？我现在亲眼看到人们在自由地生活着。” 胡适考证了这封信，从文法、标点和日期来断定，这篇文章百分之百是别人代笔。他说： “可怜我的老朋友已经没有不说话的自由了。” 胡适的判断也许只对了一半。这封信确实是别人代笔的，学生来写，由范文澜修订。但这不代表它违背陈垣的本意。胡适南下之后不久，陈垣在学生陪同下，步行十多里迎接解放军进城。日后说到给胡适写公开信那一刻，对他来说，是“由谢山转入韶山”。 谢山 指的是清代的史学家全祖望。胡适跟他通信的时候，正在研究的就是全祖望校订的《水经注》。他认为清代学者的考据与杜威思想相通：大胆假设，小心求证。 而 韶山 ，指的是毛泽东。 【毛泽东录音】 同一时期，大洋另一侧，胡适还在整理他的《水经注》，以排遣精神上的苦闷。可是他离开家的时候只带出来10册书，有两册留在了北平。 同一个夏天，胡思杜正在帮他父亲抄录这两本书。在1949年6月27日抄完，盖上印章，存入了北大的图书馆。不久，他被要求离开。 艾奇逊：美国欲以一切可行之法，鼓励中国之发展，使其成为独立且稳定之国家。 1949年8月，美国发表中美关系白皮书，认为中国内战的结果不是美国所能左右，对国民政府的批评极为严厉。艾奇逊说，中国未来的希望在于它悠久的文明和民主个人主义。 胡适跟毛泽东对此都极不满意。胡适认为，美国在中国倒下流血的时候，却说罪不在我。而毛泽东在8月14日写了社论，告诫中国民主个人主义的拥护者：丢掉幻想，准备斗争。 毛泽东：让那些内外反动派在我们面前发抖吧，让他们去说我们这也不行、那也不行吧。 他点名了胡适，说他是帝国主义及其走狗、中国反动政府只能控制的极少数知识分子之一。 同一个月，胡思杜进入华北人民革命大学，接受马列主义改造，穿上了蓝灰色的制服。 电影《思想问题》：“主任，我……我有罪，我还能不能赎罪？”“当然可以。” 他对朋友徐大春说，离开北大是因为很有压力，有一些人觉得他留在那里不方便，请他离开。他是为了安全才进了革大。 那位朋友给胡适写信，说他的儿子兴致并不高，不过很现实，过下去再说。 毛泽东录音：“中华人民共和国中央人民政府今天成立啦！” 10月1日，新时代开始。北大宿舍里的人需要跟上。 最早的是住在6号的朱光潜。一个月后，他的自我检讨登在了《人民日报》上。他说旧教育把自己培养成个人自由主义者，今后要努力学习，赶上时代跟群众。 这是中华人民共和国成立之后，《人民日报》第一份发布的知识分子检讨。 胡思杜从旁观察。他对朋友说，像朱光潜等人 lie low，内心很痛苦，他那份检讨是当局要求他写的。 住在18号的沈从文也写了一篇，题目是《给胡适之先生的一封公开信》，他劝胡适认清形势，回中国为人民服务。他的学生马逢华读过这篇文章，对他说：“你这个信的主题，好像是劝大家同归于尽，还不如不写。” 沈从文连连摇头，好像有难言之隐。这封信没有发表。 也有人找了19号的胡思杜，要他写信劝父亲回来。胡思杜托朋友给父亲带口信，说：不劝您回来，您一生努力介绍到中国的那一套，时至今日，全部被清算中。 后来在学校写检讨的时候，他把自己当初的错误态度写了进去。大意是，当他说他父亲恐怕永远不会赞成集体主义的时候，他还不懂，人是可以改造的。 儿子宣布父亲是人民的敌人，胡适说：这件事很有意思 1950年春天，胡适收到了国内友人的来信，说胡思杜已经成为了一个新人，他在学校很受欢迎，还成为了一个什么领导。见过他的亲人说他健谈了，相当的快活。他的革大同学沈育光也说他爽朗热情，满口都是前进的语气，说自己父亲是顽固分子，受到了国民党的利用。 胡思杜上学之后，家里那只波斯猫没有人管，渐渐流浪。沈虎雏看到它跟一些野猫在一起，身上的长毛很快变得杂乱了。 有一天，那只野猫在沈家生下了一窝小猫，当中有一只小黑猫，长得酷似它的父亲。沈从文用手绢把它包起来，带到了革大去，交给了炊事班的人去养。胡思杜也在这个伙房里，表现得很积极，有一天帮着切了给1000人吃的肉。沈虎雏说，不知道在那伙房里，他有没有认出自家波斯猫的后代。 沈从文在小说里写了这只小猫，猫在炊事员的肚子上吵闹，被闹醒的人细声细气地跟它说话，是父亲般的感情。这篇小说改了7次，没能发表。 沈从文的笔没有改造成功。 胡思杜顺利毕业，被分配到了唐山铁道学院马列主义研究室工作。 他搬走的第二年春天，那只波斯猫回来过。它的两个眼睛都已经瞎了，站在原来主人的房顶上叫。沈虎雏说，有人想喂它，叫它下来，但那只猫已经没有反应。 就在这一年秋天，胡适在纽约看到了报纸，他的儿子声讨他为“帝国主义走狗”以及“人民公敌”。 胡思杜的文章登在9月16号上海《大公报》的头版。他检讨过去的父子之情，称为“反动的臭虫立场”，宣布父亲是“反动阶级的忠臣”，“人民的敌人”，也是自己的敌人。 《时代》周刊迅速做了报道，并且采访了胡适。 胡适的反应是：这件事“很有意思”。他并没有觉得受到困扰。 9月28日，傅斯年投书报纸，对胡思杜以责备的方式辩护，说他从小不读书，写东西文理不通，像“人民的敌人”这样的字眼是他今生写不出来的。这篇文章是别人写的，强迫胡思杜签名。 私下里，胡适给徐大春写了一封信。他说，他相信这文章是他儿子自己写的，而且老实说，他这篇文字写得还不坏，比裴文中、冯友兰等人的自白高明多了。 冯友兰也是杜威的学生，在1949年写信给毛泽东，表示要用马克思主义立场重写《中国哲学史》。毛泽东回复：可以慢慢地改，总以采取老实态度为宜。 1944年胡思杜在美国上学的时候，五门功课中有四门不及格。胡适曾经感慨说，“看样子，正途出身是没有希望”。但在1950年，他第一次夸赞儿子的文章，写得比中国著名的大儒要高明。 日后胡适在演讲中讲到这件事时，说到《论语》：父为子隐，子为父隐，直在其中。胡适讲到他的儿子，被要求像苏联官方宣传当中的13岁的少年英雄一样，告发了自己的父亲。 胡适（录音）：Sons and daughters are required to inform against their own parents. 胡适在日记里抄下了吴南如的来信，说当年蒋介石曾经让他所在的大使馆转信，要求在苏俄的蒋经国回国。蒋经国回答：蒋介石是人民的敌人，故也是我的敌人，不愿意见他，除非在战场上。 胡适没有向外界透露，他正在被儿子批判的同时，收到了儿子的家信。这封信是在批判父亲的稿子刊出之前5天写的。他问候了父亲，说听说他前一阵子身体不太好，希望他“少见客，多保重身体”。 从目前看，只有他的革大同学沈育光写到了那段时间胡思杜的处境。他说，思杜向他吐露，学习小组当中的干部和同学常常责难他，要他批评父亲。他只好装腔作势跟父亲脱离关系，“假如不这样做的话，就有可能会有不幸发生”。 写这封信，可能是胡思杜在批判稿当中最后一句说的“还没有完全根除的非无产阶级感情”。 不过在当时的时局下，胡思杜寄出家信的时机并不寻常。一周之后，胡适在大陆的其他三位亲人，在同一天分别写信给他，都提到了思杜。胡适在日记里面记下了时间的巧合。 9月24号，他曾经在儿子的新闻剪报旁边写下一句话的分析，说这个批判稿件，应当是共产党已经知道我发表长文消息之后的反攻。 这篇长文，他指的是在《外交事务》上刊登的《斯大林大战略中的中国》。和毛泽东一样，胡适也在反驳白皮书。他认为不能把国民政府的失败只归结于自身的崩溃，这个结局和斯大林在中国的战略有关，中共军队25年的发展，就是这个战略的核心。 10月1日，胡适的文章正式刊出。同一天，斯大林电报促请中国以志愿军名义出兵朝鲜。 就在这个月底，中国人民志愿军跨过鸭绿江。1950年11月25日，毛泽东的长子毛岸英在朝鲜战场阵亡。杨尚昆日记记录了，他的父亲知道消息时，长叹一声。 抗美援朝开始之后，胡思杜在唐山的学校里自编自演反美话剧《美国之音》，积极批判父亲，觉得父亲有罪，自己是在为父亲赎罪。 去唐山之前，他已经把母亲留下的那一箱财物上交了组织，说他不再需要这些东西了。 他想加入中国共产党。他也有计划，希望在1950年结婚。 他的两个愿望都没有实现。 胡适说毛泽东是他从前的学生，毛泽东为此一夜没睡 1951年，全国知识分子思想改造运动开始。 1951年12月17日，是胡适60岁的生日，这一天也是北大53年的校庆日。胡适把批判自己的报道贴进了日记，说是“纪念北大”。 北大老教授座谈，结论是胡适是旧学术界“集反动之大成的代表人物”。北大的中文、哲学、史学、图书馆四个系，联合举行控诉胡适罪行大会。 12.24日有一篇是朱光潜批判他的文章，提到胡适说自己的儿子“没有缄默的自由”。胡适觉得，这是他儿子给很多人开了一条生路。 但是朱光潜并没有过关。此后从系里到院里，再到全校大会，他连续检讨。他的学生朱虹回忆，“一夜之间，他就满头白发”。 清华的冯友兰也屡次检查，他女儿说，“剥光了也过不了关”。金岳霖来家中探望他，进门就说：“芝生，你就交代了吧。”两个人抱头痛哭。 金岳霖是胡适曾经评价为“中国最倔强的个人主义的哲学家”。思想改造之后，他清算了自己，承认逻辑也有阶级性。 胡适（录音）：他们的苦痛，他们的不自由，都是我们国家的最大的不幸，都是国家的最大的损失。我们可以说，他们受的痛苦，就等于他们替我们的国家受痛苦，就等于替我们整个民族受痛苦。 此时在美国，人们看到的毛泽东传记当中，他是一个浪漫的诗人、书法家、文学评论者。所以1951年7月，胡适写了一篇文章，他请美国人去读一读毛泽东的《论人民民主专政》，说那是一份雄辩的、直言不讳的政治纲领，而且他正在以此统治中国。 这篇文章的题目叫《我的前学生毛泽东》。 胡适（录音）：比如毛泽东就和一批湖南青年来到北京。他们是师范学校的毕业生，无法通过大学相当严格的入学考试，因此我们允许他们旁听。 胡思杜整理的父亲的文件中，有一张1920年的明信片。那一年，毛泽东在湖南要办自修大学，登门请胡适审定章程，这个学校的校名来自胡适。此后，毛泽东写了这张明信片给胡适，说将来湖南的事，“还有多点要借重先生”。 这是一个传统的师生关系、父子关系都已经颠覆的历史时期。很快，全国高校院系调整，胡适过去的校长办公室，和毛泽东当过助理员的图书馆，都将不再是北大的一部分。在这样的时候，胡适还在将这位中国最高的执掌权力者称为他的前学生，而且一说再说。 毛泽东对此似乎很不愉快。一直到1959年4月15日，竺可桢在日记中记录，毛泽东对他说，有三个消息让他一晚上没睡着，其中之一，就是胡适“硬说毛主席是他的学生”。 毛泽东开启大批判，胡适说：野火烧不尽，春风吹又生 毛泽东（录音）：我们正在做我们的前人从来没有做过的一项光荣伟大的事业。我们的目的一定要达到，我们的目的一定能够达到。 1954年10月，这一次，毛泽东亲自开启对于胡适思想的斗争。刚开始的界定是古典文学领域，很快扩大。 中科院院长郭沫若说，胡适在政治上是头等战犯，但在某些人心目中还是学术界的孔子，没有打倒。中国科学院跟作协召开联席会议，决定从九个领域全面批判胡适，后来又加上了禅宗研究，成为了十大罪状。 1948年录像当中，研究生物学的武兆发教授，也需要批判自己的资产阶级唯心论。因为《人民日报》说，胡适的实验主义哲学，还像幽灵一样附在知识分子的身上。 胡适：我相信一个自由独立的人，对于思想，对于一切思想，一切主义，一切信仰，必须先要经过一个怀疑，而后可以相信，必须仔细考究过，而后可以相信。 这一年，有一个叫郎玉珠的学生在唐山铁道学院读书，她的老师是胡思杜。她说，胡老师给她最深的印象，就是革命的决心。上课的时候主动批判自己的父亲，私下也经常说：“咱们这些旧社会过来的人，要好好地改造自己的思想。” 胡思杜一直没有结婚。他的亲人说，女孩听到介绍的时候，一听是战犯的名字，就不愿意接触他。 1955年，胡适读到了罗尔纲批判他的文章。 中国有私人师承的传统，资助家境贫寒的弟子。20年前，胡适让罗尔纲住在家中，给思杜上课，指导他研究太平天国。1931年，罗尔纲给胡适写信说：“一个行尸走肉的青年，居然在先生栽培之下复活起来。” 20多年后，罗尔纲在批判稿中写，因为听信胡适的话，他的前半生只有灰冷幻灭、悲哀虚无，成了行尸走肉活死人。 几百万字的批判稿里面，多数批判的是胡适的思想，而这篇批判稿，批判的是过去的感情。批判稿的题目叫《两个人生》。 胡适：没有保持沉默的自由，我的朋友、学生都必须出来驳斥和谴责我。他们十分清楚，我一定能够理解：他们没有保持沉默的自由。 一个人理解，不等于他没有感受。 胡适在纽约，曾经指着罗尔纲在40年代写给他的那本充满了师生之情的旧书，对唐德刚说：“你看他现在这样批判我。”唐德刚说：“说不定他的思想已经真正搞通了呢。”胡适说：“胡说，胡说。”他连连摇头，说：“不可能，不可能。” 罗尔纲在文章中写道，他看了胡适儿子的文章之后“豁然开朗”，说“父子还可以划清敌我界限，我做学生的更可以和老师划清敌我界限了。” 1958年，罗尔纲入了党。同一年，胡适在台湾重新出版了罗尔纲当年这本旧书，把它改为《师门五年记》。他把这本40年代的书作为生日礼物，分赠给朋友，说这本旧书比他30多个荣誉博士学位更值得光荣。 这本旧书，也许就是他说的学者的兵器。那里有情感的证据，学问的证据，人性的证据。不论后来发生什么事，改变不了历史的真实。 胡适（录音）：我相信他们清算历史是不会成功，是要打失败的。古人有两句诗说得很好，这两句诗：野火烧不尽，春风吹又生。 毛泽东说批判片面了，请他回来，胡适问：除了思想，什么是我？ 1956年，胡思杜突然变了。根据学生的转述，年初他忽然活跃起来，有时候竟然议论时政，对朋友说：“中共批判我父亲实在不够资格。世界上几十个大学给我父亲博士学位，共产党说他是伪学者，那么其他国家的人大概是瞎了眼。” 这些话未必字字可靠，不过后来批判他的官方文件中确实写着，他说胡思杜“仍然仰慕父亲的反动才华”，向别人谈起父亲得到过很多博士学位。 活跃的并不是胡思杜一个人。1956年是费孝通所说的“知识分子的早春”。1月，周恩来在会议上说，工业化和科学发展离不开知识分子。2月，赫鲁晓夫在苏共二十大上揭露斯大林时期的个人崇拜和大清洗。顾准记得，中央党校传达这个报告的时候，“举座是可怕的寂静”。 两个月之后，毛泽东提出团结一切力量搞建设，艺术上百花齐放，学术上百家争鸣。 毛泽东，八大开幕词：团结全党，团结国内外一切可能团结的力量，为了建设一个伟大的社会主义的中国而奋斗。 毛泽东讲话同一个月，陈垣接受了外交部顾问之托，写信给胡适，劝他回国看看。信中讲：“这些对于你是对你的思想，并不是对你个人。你如果回去，一定还是受欢迎。” 胡适在这句话底下画了线，在旁边写： “除了思想之外，什么是我？” 8年前毛泽东留他的时候，他说：“他们要我吗？”现在这句话，算是一个解释。 1957年2月份，毛泽东公开表态说：“我们刚开始批判胡适很好，后来有点片面性了，把胡适的一切全部抹杀了。”要求以后要写一两篇文章补救一下。 一个月之后，胡适收到了香港报人曹聚仁的信，请他回国。此前，曹聚仁刚刚在北京见过了周恩来和毛泽东。胡适没有回复这封信。 几天之后，他又收到他儿子的来信，这是7年来的第一封。日记中，他没有摘录内容。信看起来是写给母亲的，因为信的末尾说，另有一信给父亲，已经寄出。但是胡适自始至终没有收到过那封信。他怀疑，是有人安排思杜给他写信，但又改变了计划。 4月14日，周恩来选择直接说话。他说，胡适是典型的资产阶级思想，还要批判，但是，如果他今天愿意回来为社会主义服务，他还可以讲他的实验主义。 同一天，《人民日报》刊登了朱光潜的新文章。8年前，朱光潜开启了中国知识分子在报纸上发表检讨的先河，现在他又被当成了响应百家争鸣的先锋。 朱光潜写道，他这五六年当中，口是封住了，心里不服。现在他开了口，说想要说服他，就得自己懂，而且拿出道理来。只不过，这篇文章当中好像已经提前公布了结果，他断言，头脑当中的战胜一方，一定是马列主义。 57年4月，沈从文在上海的报纸上，看到了巴金、曹禺等人的鸣放。他说一片抱怨声，他不以为然，跟妻子写信说：真的鸣，应当是拿出有分量的作品，由万千读者来裁断，他们比少数人要公道和正确得多。 胡适（录音）：我们当初要的是，没有人在背后用鞭子打你，没有人在辅导你，没有人在监督你，人人都自由，本他的良心，本他的知识，充分用他的材料，用他的自由——创作的自由来创作。 五一当天，《人民日报》发出整风的通知，邀请党外人士给共产党提意见。当天上海20万人上街游行。 沈从文画了一张小画，在人海的边上，有一只孤单的小船。他说：锣鼓的海，红旗的海，船在做梦。在括号里写了一句： 总而言之不醒。 《人民日报》很快刊登了胡思杜的意见。他说，教师们希望有一位教授来担任院长，提了两年没有批准。胡思杜认为，原因是领导不了解知识分子。他们希望有一个教授当院长，就像少数民族希望有他们自己人当自治区主席一样。 他的父亲在1922年也曾经这样说过，北大的根本变化，是从校长学长的独裁制，变为了教授治校制。 就在胡思杜的意见发表前5天，毛泽东开始写《事情正在起变化》。他说：现在右派的进攻还没有达到顶点，他们越猖狂，对我们越有利益。 5月23日起，唐山市委连续邀请教师们座谈，由市委书记主持。胡思杜依然在说。根据官方材料记录他鸣放阶段的发言，他认为院长、秘书、助理这些岗位集中在党员手里，专业负责人难有实际的权力；苏联的教学大纲导致课业的压力太大，很多学生累病了；他们对政治课也有意见。 5月30日，陈垣在座谈会上说：“士可杀不可辱。老教授一次次检讨被斗争，有时候人家原是热爱国家的，但都指着脸骂人家是反革命。” 第二天，影片当中的武兆发也发了言。他批评教育部的领导不懂业务，主观自信。 知识分子在开口讲话，整整讲了一个月。6月5日开会讨论学校建设的时候，门口、楼上、窗外都站满了人。 胡适，联合国演讲：这一个月的自由假期，1957年5月8日开始，6月7日戛然而止。 毛泽东发动反右；父亲说儿子没有不说话的自由，这一次，胡思杜选择不说话 6月8日，毛泽东起草党内指示《组织力量反击右派分子的猖狂进攻》，《人民日报》发表社论《这是为什么？》，反击开始。 胡思杜看到了，但此后他接受新华社采访，公开反对《人民日报》的做法。作为唐院民盟秘书，他对记者说，唐山的十句话只说了两句，还有四五句没有讲，而且是更重要的话。他还引用了一位老教授的话，说：“我这个铁树还未开花。” 胡思杜不是没有恐惧，因为他接受采访的时候说，他担忧有人会用过去右派的法宝再来压我们。但是他仍然指责《人民日报》，新的定性会影响民盟团结，让大家感觉不到“共同监督”的味道。这四个字是曾经毛泽东做出的公开承诺。 毛泽东（录音）：同志们，今天在座的，还有我们国内各民主党派和无党派民主人士的代表…… 7月1日，《人民日报》社论发表，把此前的鸣放称为“阳谋”。 毛泽东（录音）：他们是和我们一道工作的亲密的朋友，他们给了我们很多的帮助，我们对他们表示热烈的欢迎。 7月15日，河北省委整风办公室上报材料：胡思杜是唐院的主要斗争对象。从7月开始，唐山铁道学院用大字报、漫画、广播批判胡思杜，通过小组座谈要求他彻底交代。 在同一个月，武兆发教授被划为右派。他用做实验的生物解剖刀结束了生命。北京师范大学召开全校大会继续批判他，批判他的人中，有他的校长陈垣。 胡适，联合国演讲：于是，“百花齐放、百家争鸣”运动突然变成迫害、清洗“右派”的运动。这场运动在中国大陆仍在进行，十几位知名知识分子被选作公开审讯、迫害、羞辱和贬斥的对象。 这场运动中，全国超过55万人被划为右派。 这样的批判，胡思杜经受了两个多月。 此前，胡适曾经说他的儿子没有不说话的自由。现在，胡思杜选择不说话。 文件这样形容他：胡思杜现在采取“包下来”和“躺下去”的办法，一切大帽子都戴，就是不交代自己的具体活动，尤其与民盟之间有关人员的关系。 根据辗转传到香港的消息，唐山铁道学院的学生同情胡思杜的言论，认为他深得人心，这使唐院的反右迟迟未能顺利开展。官方文件要求进一步动员中间力量，更有力地展开斗争。 一个多月之后，《河北日报》报道，老教授史家宜这棵“铁树”开了花，他揭发胡思杜挑拨党和知识分子的关系。 8月21日，《人民日报》发文，点名胡思杜参与卑鄙篡夺学校的领导权。 第二天，《光明日报》发文说，“美帝国主义走狗胡适的儿子”进步都是伪装，表面划清父子界限，思想始终没有改造。文章引用了胡思杜在唐山市委座谈会上的话作为铁证，他说： “在学院中，党只有威而无信。” 这篇文章的题目是《继承胡适衣钵的胡思杜》。 七年前被要求划清的父子界限，就这样被组织恢复了。而多年来一直被认为是不成器的儿子，胡思杜第一次也是最后一次被外界认定，继承了他父亲胡适的衣钵。 胡适：真理使你自由，真理使你独立；热爱真理、热爱寻找真理，会使一个人自由而独立。 儿子写下遗书，五天后，父亲在联合国向中国知识分子致敬 1957年9月3日，唐山铁道学院举行了3000多人的反右批判大会。报纸说，胡思杜的右派言行激起了师生员工的无比愤怒，已经召开了数十次大小会议进行揭发和批判。 4天之后，路透社报道，当时曾经发生过学生罢课的汉阳，有3人被判死刑。胡适在联合国演讲中引用了这则消息： 胡适，联合国演讲：我们谨向他们所有人表示衷心的同情和崇高的敬意。 他做这个演讲的5天前，胡思杜写下了遗书。 他的信留给堂兄胡思孟，一位工人。胡思孟赶到唐山的时候，看到满院的大字报，批判胡适父子。遗书的原件没有交给他，他抄了一份。他记得，信开头说： “我已经没有别的亲人了，只有你。” 其实他还有别的亲人，那些共产党员、知识分子。但思孟认为，弟弟是怕连累别人，自己是工人，出身好一些。 胡思杜把钱和手表留给了他，希望能够用来供孩子们读书上大学。 官方没有公布胡思杜的死讯。胡思孟在郊外找了一个地方，安葬了36岁的弟弟，立下一块小木牌，带走了一车弟弟生前的书。在有的书上，他认出了胡适的名字。 胡适对蒋介石说：总统，你错了；他死后，毛泽东未置一词 1958年3月，胡适在日记里贴下一则新闻。那篇报道说，思杜被送去了劳动改造，下乡耕田。剪报边上，这位父亲没有写下任何批注。 一个月之后，胡适从美国去了台湾，出任中央研究院院长。在4月10号的就职典礼上，他和蒋介石发生了冲突。 蒋介石谈到胡适参加领导的新文化运动，打倒孔家店。根据在场的陈仲玉回忆，蒋介石认为，五四提倡的自由主义，可能给了共产党兴起的机会。 胡适当场反驳，说：“总统，你错了。” 根据在场者回忆，胡适说，打倒孔家店，是打倒它的权威性和神秘性。世界上任何学说，任何思想，只要是不允许怀疑、不允许批评的，我都要打倒。一个自由的国家，不是一般奴才能够造成功的。 胡适（录音）：自由，自由，能够自由的人，爱自由如生命，爱自由如面包，爱自由比面包还重要，比生命还重要。只有这一种的人，才可以造成一个自由的国家。 蒋介石当晚失眠，他写，这是平生所受的第二次大横逆。 两天之后，他宴请中研院院士，说1948年是我派飞机接出了胡适跟梅贻琦，才脱离了北平的危困。蒋介石特别留意了胡适的脸，说他毫不在乎，面无表情。 1948年胡适离开北平的时候，他离开的不只是危困。他离开他的大学，他离开他的朋友，他离开他的学生，他离开他的儿子。 大约在那一年的最后一天，他和傅斯年在南京一边喝酒，一边背诵陶渊明的诗： 种桑长江边，三年望当采。 枝条始欲茂，忽值山河改。 柯叶自摧折，根株浮沧海。 春蚕既无食，寒衣欲谁待。 本不植高原，今日复何悔。 两人相对，落下泪来。 1958年，毛泽东发动大跃进，6亿人改造山河。 5月，苏雪林写信给胡适，说她听说了胡思杜自杀身亡的消息。胡适很快回信，说这是谣言。几个月之前，还有朋友传来消息，说他儿子被送到了东北。他还专门给江冬秀打了个长途电话，让她不要信这样的谣言。 胡适做了一辈子的考据，如果一个消息跟另一个消息对不上，他就还可以等。 大陆的饥荒当中，胡适对秘书提到了沈从文、朱光潜，说听说他们过得非常苦。胡适突然说： “1958年3月之后，再没有思杜的信息来。恐怕……不可免了。” 他这句话说得非常平淡，就像是自言自语。 半个月之后是母亲节，他忽然说起15年前的一次父亲节。 那一天，胡适在横渡太平洋的轮船上睡不着。他想起来当天是胡思杜的毕业日，他知道成绩不会理想，在日记里写，自己非常惭愧，作为三个孩子的父亲，没有能够尽到应尽的责任。 他一直跟孩子聚少离多。胡思杜4岁的时候，他妈妈写信告诉爸爸：“小三每天早上起来要找爸爸，晚上也要找你，常常的愁哭起来。” 现在20年过去了。他起身给儿子发了一个电报，写： “Congratulations! Whatever happens today, my love. Father.” 中国家庭的父子之间很少说爱，他写的是英文。 胡思杜没有回。胡适后来才知道，那个学期，他儿子根本没去上课，把父亲汇来的钱用去赌马，身边的东西都已经典当光了，包括父亲送他的打字机。 胡适讲这件事情的最后一句是： “后来他回来了，我也没有责备他。” 九个月之后，胡适心脏病去世。他的遗嘱中，一直有胡思杜的名字。 新闻片：新文化运动的领导人胡适博士突然因心脏病复发，不幸逝世……蒋总统也亲临凭吊。 胡适去世之后，蒋介石在日记中写，“胡适之死，对革命事业和民族复兴的建国思想来说，消除了障碍。” 而毛泽东对胡适未置一词。经年累月的大批判之后，如果胡适是障碍，他早已经被抹去。 文革开始，胡家父子的笔迹被一把火烧掉 四年之后，文革开始。 郭沫若的两个儿子相继在运动中死去，他用毛笔一字一字抄了儿子郭世英的日记。 沈虎雏把他父亲的信毁了，日后从老房子的垃圾里，一张一张找回他的字。 胡思孟把有胡适父子笔迹的书都烧了。他抄的那封遗书还剩了一角，写着： “好好学习，为社会主义立点功。” 此时，胡思杜的墓地和那块木牌都已经消失。 长子胡祖望一直在海外生活，去世之后，他的骨灰安葬在父母身边。旁边，是他为弟弟立的一块空碑。 凌叔华曾经以他们兄弟俩为原型，写过一篇小说，叫《小哥儿俩》。 故事里面，这个哥哥教八哥念书，他逗弟弟说：“八哥念得比你好。”弟弟没有不高兴，因为他爸爸也常常说他念书不如哥哥。他总是笑嘻嘻地说：“那我教八哥唱歌。” 这只八哥被一只野猫吃了。兄弟俩哭了一场，约好第二天一早去报仇。 清晨，弟弟拿着鸡毛掸子进了院子。草叶上都是露水，他跟着麻雀蹦蹦跳跳，渐渐地忘记了自己来做什么。突然，他在墙角看到一个破箱子，里面是那只野猫和它刚刚出生的孩子。他叫哥哥来找棉花垫一个窝，摸着那只小猫说： “哥哥，你看它的小鼻子多好玩，还出着热气。” 那是一个小黑猫，有一个红鼻子。

title: The Nvidia Scandal Exposes American Blind Spots
zh_title: 英伟达丑闻暴露美国盲点
source: 欧洲政策分析中心 （CEPA） - CEPA
summary: 华盛顿已经建立了一个复杂的出口管制和许可要求网络，以防止人工智能芯片进入中国。然而，英伟达创始人黄仁勋与被指控向北京传递信息的中国女商人黄爱丽之间明显的“美人计”事件，不仅仅是这些控制措施的盲点问题。它讲述了在全球化、互联的世界中关闭先进技术的困难，以及一家公司、监管机构和行政部门看到了警告信号却迟迟未采取行动。如果现有规则得到执行，Nvidia
content:
华盛顿已经建立了一个复杂的出口管制和许可要求网络，以防止人工智能芯片进入中国。然而，英伟达创始人黄仁勋与被指控向北京传递信息的中国女商人黄爱丽之间明显的“美人计”事件，不仅仅是这些控制措施的盲点问题。它讲述了在全球化、互联的世界中关闭先进技术的困难，以及一家公司、监管机构和行政部门看到了警告信号却迟迟未采取行动。如果现有规则得到执行，英伟达就不应该向总部位于新加坡的云计算公司 Megaspeed International 出售先进芯片。 Alice Huang 是 Megaspeed 的高管，该公司成为 Nvidia 的主要客户，并因可能违反美国出口管制而受到审查。英伟达董事会已聘请外部顾问来调查中国情报部门是否针对其前首席执行官，后者在其事务曝光后辞职。该公司坚称，没有理由相信其机密或国家安全受到损害。这个故事的核心是供应链的不透明性，而它始于 Megaspeed 错综复杂的所有权。该公司于2015年在新加坡注册成立，名称为第七大道国际，是中国网络游戏行业中的新兴企业。它于 2023 年采用现名。
同年晚些时候，Megaspeed 的股份通过一家在英属维尔京群岛注册的公司转让给另一家在新加坡注册的公司 Swiftdata。谁最终控制 Swiftdata 目前尚不清楚。错综复杂的注册流程并不能证明国家控制，中国投资也不等同于中国政府所有权。但中国的国有资本和私人资本经常通过子公司、控股公司和离岸工具进行流动。 Megaspeed 复杂的企业历史本应引发严格审查，审查谁控制该公司以及谁最终将从其购买美国芯片中受益。尽管存在警告信号，Megaspeed 仍成为 Nvidia 的官方云合作伙伴，并购买了价值数十亿美元的先进计算设备。其印度尼西亚子公司进口了最先进的 Nvidia 硬件。美国当局已调查Megaspeed是否也帮助中国客户获得Nvidia芯片。 Megaspeed 否认非法转让，也没有任何公开调查结果证实存在出口管制违规行为。但英伟达面临的问题从来不是违规行为是否得到证实；而是问题。问题在于具有这种特征的客户是否值得信任和访问。 2025 年 8 月，Nvidia 总法律顾问通过电子邮件向负责调查 Megaspeed 的部门特工发送电子邮件，称商务部高级官员已批准此次外展活动。调查已暂停并移交给司法部。
其他机构提议将 Megaspeed 添加到被认为对美国国家安全构成风险的外国企业和组织的实体名单中。商务部从未这样做过。官员们敦促商务部采取行动，国务卿马可·卢比奥 (Marco Rubio) 于 2026 年 5 月向商务部长霍华德·卢特尼克 (Howard Lutnick) 发送了一份有关 Megaspeed 的备忘录。据报道，财政部长斯科特·贝森特 (Scott Bessent) 最近与卢特尼克对质，问道：“Megaspeed 为何不在实体名单上？”商务部否认发生过交易。白宫收到警告。据报道，唐纳德·特朗普总统去年年底听取了简报和一份关于爱丽丝的机密备忘录

【原文 English Original】
Washington has built an elaborate web of export controls and licensing requirements to keep artificial intelligence chips from reaching China. Yet Nvidia founder Jensen Huang’s apparent “honeytrap” affair with Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman accused of passing information to Beijing, is about more than the blind spots of those controls. It is about the difficulty of shutting down access to advanced tech in a globalized, interconnected world — and about a company, a regulator, and an executive branch that saw warning signs and were slow act on them. Had existing rules been enforced, Nvidia should never have been selling advanced chips to the Singapore-based cloud computing company Megaspeed International. Alice Huang was an executive at Megaspeed, which became a major Nvidia customer, and attracted scrutin y over possible violations of American export controls. Nvidia’s board has retained outside counsel to investigate whether Chinese intelligence targeted their former CEO, who resigned after his affairs were revealed. The company maintains that it has no reason to believe its secrets or national security were compromised. At its core, the story is about the opacity of supply chains, and it begins with Megaspeed’s convoluted ownership. The company incorporated in Singapore in 2015 as 7Road International, emerging from the Chinese online gaming industry. It adopted its current name in 2023. Later that year, Megaspeed’s shares were transferred , through a company registered in the British Virgin Islands, to another Singapore-registered company, Swiftdata. Who ultimately controls Swiftdata remains unclear. Convoluted incorporation trails do not prove state control, and Chinese investment is not synonymous with Chinese government ownership. But state-linked and private Chinese capital often  moves  through subsidiaries, holding companies, and offshore vehicles. Megaspeed’s complex corporate history should have triggered rigorous scrutiny of who controlled the firm and who would ultimately benefit from its purchases of US chips.  Despite the warning signs, Megaspeed became an official Nvidia cloud partner and purchased billions of dollars’ worth of advanced computing equipment. Its Indonesian subsidiary imported cutting-edge Nvidia hardware. US authorities have investigated whether Megaspeed also helped Chinese customers obtain Nvidia chips. Megaspeed has denied illicit transfers, and no public finding has established an export-control violation. But the question for Nvidia was never whether a violation had been proven; it was whether a customer with this profile warranted trust and access. In August 2025, Nvidia’s general counsel  emailed  Department agents investigating Megaspeed, saying that a senior Commerce official had approved the outreach. The investigation was paused and transferred to the Justice Department.  Other agencies proposed adding Megaspeed to the entity list of foreign businesses and organizations that are deemed to pose a risk to US national security. Commerce never did. Officials  pressed  Commerce to act, and Secretary of State Marco Rubio sent Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick a memorandum on Megaspeed in May 2026. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent recently reportedly  confronted  Lutnik, asking: “How come Megaspeed isn’t on the entities list?” Commerce denies that the  exchange  took place. The White House was warned. President Donald Trump was reportedly briefed late last year and a classified memorandum on Alice Huang circulated among senior officials before his May visit to China. Apparently, no action was taken. Instead, Nvidia CEO Huang joined the presidential delegation to Beijing and, in September, attended the White House state dinner for Chinese President Xi Jinping. Jensen Huang’s own conduct compounded the failure. An executive with his access to the president and to sensitive policy discussions carries a responsibility that goes beyond his obligations to shareholders. A relationship with a foreign national linked to a customer under federal investigation was, at best, reckless. Washington depends on companies such as Nvidia to sustain its technological lead over China, expand domestic computing capacity, and support an increasingly AI-dependent defense posture. Yet these companies  remain  commercial enterprises that  are  accountable to shareholders and driven by incentives that might not always align with national security objectives.  Get the Latest Sign US export controls focus on where advanced chips are shipped, yet access to computing power no longer requires owning the hardware.  Renting “offshore” computing is often legal. A Chinese company banned from purchasing certain advanced US processors may be able to buy computing capacity from servers in another jurisdiction. Megaspeed reportedly  provided computing services to Chinese technology customers, including the Chinese e-commerce leader Alibaba. This gap risks widening as AI infrastructure expands across Southeast Asia, the Middle East, and other regions. The US needs to enforce existing rules and close the gaps. First, that means applying export controls consistently. When the evidence warrants, enforcement must be separated from corporate lobbying — and acted on. Second, add access to advanced computing power to export controls, not just the chips themselves. That means know- your-customer  requirements for cloud providers and close monitoring of overseas cloud infrastructure. Third, invest in systematic mapping of corporate ownership and financial networks. Screening named entities is insufficient when relationships extend across holding companies, investment vehicles, and multiple jurisdictions. Chipmakers should be expected to know who ultimately owns their customers. Fourth, establish clear security expectations and channels for intelligence-sharing with executives at the commanding heights of American technology. Congress is preparing to act. Top Republican and Democratic lawmakers hope to  include  three proposed measures toughening rules on exporting AI chips. Three House committee chairs have  demanded  a closed-door briefing from Huang.  His resignation should not end the inquiry. Congress should examine not only whether sensitive information was compromised, but how Megaspeed won Nvidia’s trust, why Commerce never acted, and why intelligence warnings to the executive branch failed to translate into meaningful action. The US has spent years building the tools to control what crosses its borders. But tools are only as strong as the institutions that wield them. title: Burma Junta Bombs Maternity Clinic and Bridge in Rakhine State, Killing at Least 12 Civilians, Including a Newborn
zh_title: 缅甸军政府轰炸若开邦产科诊所和桥梁，造成至少 12 名平民死亡，其中包括一名新生儿
summary: 军政府的空袭导致若开邦的众多平民死亡，缅甸军队在那里拥有完全的空中优势，可以从中国和俄罗斯购买喷气燃料。照片由 AA 信息台提供。 11 月 1 日，缅甸军方对若开邦四个乡镇的一个临时产科诊所、一座公路桥梁和村庄发动空袭，造成至少 12 名平民死亡，其中包括一名一周大的女婴。据控制该邦大部分地区的民族武装组织若开军（AA）称，另有 32 人受伤。宝宝第二天就该回家了。她的双胞胎幸存

军政府的空袭导致若开邦的众多平民死亡，缅甸军队在那里拥有完全的空中优势，可以从中国和俄罗斯购买喷气燃料。照片由 AA 信息台提供。 11 月 1 日，缅甸军方对若开邦四个乡镇的一个临时产科诊所、一座公路桥梁和村庄发动空袭，造成至少 12 名平民死亡，其中包括一名一周大的女婴。据控制该邦大部分地区的民族武装组织若开军（AA）称，另有 32 人受伤。宝宝第二天就该回家了。她的双胞胎幸存下来。妙乌的一名救援人员瓦伊洪昂 (Wai Hun Aung) 告诉路透社，这名婴儿“在爆炸中倒塌的建筑物中被压死”。根据若开通讯社 Narinjara 发布的 AA 数据，下午 5 点 27 分左右，两架战斗机在妙乌临时妇产诊所附近投下了四枚集束炸弹。袭击造成五人死亡、九人受伤，其中包括医务人员。据机管局称，下午 5 点 25 分左右，即诊所罢工前两分钟，一架战斗机轰炸了皎都镇的 Yoe Chaung 大桥，造成 7 名行人死亡、7 人受伤。当地消息人士称，位于若开邦的媒体发展媒体集团 (DMG) 受伤人数较多，有 10 人受伤。 420 英尺长的贝利桥承载着皎都和波那均之间的仰光-实兑高速公路。 “这座桥已经完全毁坏，无法通行，”一位检查这座桥的居民告诉 DMG。
袭击关闭了高速公路，乘客必须在该处换乘开往皎都、妙乌和波纳金的车辆。11 月 1 日早些时候，另外两起袭击造成平民受伤。凌晨 3 点 58 分，一架 Y-12 运输机轰炸了包都镇和包都镇的 Ywa Chaung Gyi 村，造成 5 人受伤。下午 5 点左右，两架喷气式飞机轰炸了皎漂镇的 Sane Min Pyin 村，造成 11 人受伤，房屋受损。若开邦的孕妇表示，她们现在不敢寻求医疗护理。 “由于空袭不断发生，我不敢去医院，”妙乌镇 Teinnyo 村的一名孕妇在缅甸新闻国际转载的一份报告中告诉 DMG。 2025 年 12 月 10 日，军政府对妙乌医院发动空袭，造成 33 人死亡、76 人受伤。据路透社报道，在诊所空袭前大约一个月，对皎都镇和蓬那均镇流离失所平民营地的空袭造成至少 58 人死亡。 11 月 2 日，一架军用旋翼机向皎漂镇 Sa Nae Min Pyin 村附近的一个国内流离失所者营地投下两枚炸弹，造成两名流离失所的平民死亡，五人受伤。营地内的几个避难所遭到损坏或毁坏。 11 月 1 日对若开邦的空袭是更广泛的空袭浪潮的一部分。据克伦尼人权组织称，10 月 31 日，克伦邦垒固一所学校在上课时遭到空袭，造成 3 名学生死亡、5 人受伤。
10月29日至11月1日，伊洛瓦底江军政府在缅甸境内发动了9次空袭，造成16人死亡、51人受伤。其中一半以上的空袭发生在若开邦。 11 月 1 日的袭击发生在东盟特使、菲律宾外交大臣玛丽亚·特蕾莎·拉扎罗抵达缅甸进行为期三天的人道主义访问三天后。军政府将其行动描述为针对恐怖分子的合法行动。 8 月，联合国调查人员指责军方故意以民用建筑为目标，包括学校和

Junta airstrikes have killed numerous civilians in Arakan State, where Burma’s (Myanmar’s) military has complete air superiority and can buy jet fuel from China and Russia. Photo courtesy of the AA Info Desk. A week-old baby girl was among at least 12 civilians killed on Nov. 1 when Burma’s military launched airstrikes on a temporary maternity clinic , a highway bridge and villages in four townships of Rakhine State. Thirty-two others were wounded, according to the Arakan Army (AA), the ethnic armed group that controls most of the state. The baby was due to go home the next day. Her twin survived. Wai Hun Aung, an aid worker based in Mrauk-U, told Reuters the baby was “crushed and killed when the building collapsed from the blast.” According to AA figures published by Narinjara , a Rakhine news agency, two fighter jets dropped four cluster bombs near the temporary maternity clinic in Mrauk-U at about 5:27 p.m. The strike killed five people and wounded nine, including medical staff. At about 5:25 p.m., two minutes before the clinic strike, a fighter jet bombed the Yoe Chaung Bridge in Kyauktaw Township, killing seven pedestrians and wounding seven others, according to the AA. Local sources gave Development Media Group (DMG), a Rakhine-based outlet, a higher count of 10 wounded. The 420-foot Bailey bridge carried the Yangon–Sittwe Highway between Kyauktaw and Ponnagyun. “The bridge is completely wrecked and impassable,” a resident who inspected it told DMG. The strike closed the highway at a point where boat passengers transfer to vehicles bound for Kyauktaw, Mrauk-U and Ponnagyun. Two other strikes wounded civilians earlier on Nov. 1. At 3:58 a.m., a Y-12 transport aircraft bombed Pauktaw town and Ywa Chaung Gyi village in Pauktaw Township, wounding five people. Around 5 p.m., two jets bombed Sane Min Pyin village in Kyaukphyu Township, wounding 11 people and damaging homes. Pregnant women in Rakhine say they are now afraid to seek medical care. “As airstrikes keep happening, I am terrified to go to the hospital,” a pregnant woman from Teinnyo village in Mrauk-U Township told DMG in a report republished by Burma News International. On Dec. 10, 2025, a junta airstrike on Mrauk-U Hospital killed 33 people and wounded 76. About a month before the clinic strike, airstrikes on camps for displaced civilians in Kyauktaw and Ponnagyun townships killed at least 58 people, according to Reuters. On Nov. 2, a military gyrocopter dropped two bombs on a camp for internally displaced people near Sa Nae Min Pyin village in Kyaukphyu Township, killing two displaced civilians and wounding five others . Several shelters in the camp were damaged or destroyed. The Nov. 1 strikes in Rakhine were part of a wider wave of airstrikes. On Oct. 31, an airstrike hit a school in Loikaw, Kayah (Karenni) State, while classes were in session, killing three students and wounding five, according to the Karenni Human Rights Group. The Irrawaddy recorded nine junta airstrikes across Burma from Oct. 29 to Nov. 1, killing 16 people and wounding 51. More than half of the strikes were in Rakhine State. The Nov. 1 strikes came three days after ASEAN Special Envoy Maria Theresa Lazaro, the Philippine foreign secretary, arrived in Burma for a three-day humanitarian visit . The junta has described its operations as a legitimate campaign against terrorists. In August, United Nations investigators accused the military of deliberately targeting civilian buildings, including schools and hospitals, in airstrikes. Burma’s foreign ministry responded that the military uses maximum restraint to avoid harming civilians. The junta’s air campaign relies on imported jet fuel. Burma imported more than 109,000 tonnes of aviation fuel in 2025, up 69% from the previous year and the highest volume since the 2021 coup, according to Amnesty International . From the first Iranian fuel delivery in October 2024 through the end of 2025, the military carried out 1,022 airstrikes on civilian targets. BNI-Myanmar Peace Monitor counted at least 1,728 civilians killed in military airstrikes over the same period. UN Special Rapporteur Tom Andrews said the fuel “is literally fueling mass atrocities.” Iran became the junta’s main supplier of jet fuel. Two U.S.-sanctioned tankers, Reef and Noble , delivered about 175,000 tons in nine shipments between October 2024 and December 2025, earning Iran an estimated $123 million, Reuters reported in January. In December 2025, Reef delivered about 113,000 barrels of Iranian jet fuel under a $15.8 million contract that falsely described the cargo as South African diesel, according to a Reuters investigation published Oct. 26. In a Nov. 30, 2025, letter, Burma’s foreign exchange regulator said it would issue import documents using the same description. Dynamic Wave brokered the purchase for National Energy Prime Aviation Services, a company partly owned by the military-backed government. Justice for Myanmar , which obtained the documents, identified six cargoes disguised this way and worth a combined $109.5 million. Reuters reported that Iranian fuel shipments continued in 2026 and that the military also received support from China, India and Russia. Calls to cut off the junta’s jet fuel supply have so far led to one national ban. In April 2024, the UN Human Rights Council urged member states to stop supplying jet fuel to Burma’s military. Every council member except China backed the resolution. Canada remains the only country to ban the export, sale, supply and shipment of aviation fuel to Burma, according to Justice for Myanmar. The National Unity Government, Burma’s exiled civilian government, has called for a total ban on jet fuel sales even if it grounds civilian flights. In a February 2026 letter , 235 civil society groups urged the Human Rights Council to support targeted sanctions on aviation fuel. In Washington, the House passed the BRAVE Burma Act by unanimous consent on Feb. 9. The bill would require the president to determine each year whether foreign companies operating in Burma’s jet fuel sector should face sanctions. The post Burma Junta Bombs Maternity Clinic and Bridge in Rakhine State, Killing at Least 12 Civilians, Including a Newborn appeared first on The Gateway Pundit .

听这篇文章：亲爱的，我们今天聚集在这里，度过这个叫做生活的事情。 ―  黄仁勋王子，Nvidia 首席执行官，1993 年至 2026 年 黄仁勋于 2026 年 11 月 12 日星期四辞去 Nvidia 首席执行官职务。自 1993 年 4 月 5 日创立该公司以来，他一直担任该公司首席执行官。黄的退出名义上是因为与一名可能是或不是中国间谍的买家以及至少两名公司员工有染，最终是因为英伟达被当权者视为国防承包商，而黄则从未做出调整。在这方面，黄是他自己成功的最终受害者。 Nvidia 的第一款显卡只是将三角形转换为像素。 2001 年的 GeForce 3 引入了可编程像素着色器，这意味着显卡的功能不再是预先定义的。然而，几乎让这家公司丧命的杀手锏是 2006 年推出的 CUDA，它是一个用于对这些着色器进行编程的 API。在接下来 16 年的大部分时间里，黄仁勋兜售 CUDA 的福音，坚信它是未来加速计算的平台；然后，在 2022 年，ChatGPT 出现了。 ChatGPT 明确了 GPU 最有用的用途：大型语言模型，而 Nvidia 制造了最好的 GPU。
不仅如此，黄仁勋还意识到，加速计算的未来不仅仅是芯片，而是系统；这推动了 2019 年对 Mellanox 的收购，这为 Nvidia 提供了从芯片进行横向扩展的技术，使其成为大规模训练的最佳选择，从而使大型语言模型成为可能。为此 Nvidia 收取了非常高的价格，利润率超过 70%，因为他们可以：他们拥有平台、技术，而且在过去几年中，当其他人试图制造自己的芯片时，他们拥有供应链。黄对亚洲供应链的影响尤其不容小觑。伯恩·霍巴特（Byrne Hobart）在他的著作《繁荣：泡沫和停滞的终结》中指出，泡沫的好处之一是它们提供了协调功能，因为对错过的恐惧会激励具有相互关联的依赖关系的多个实体同时致力于建设；黄在很多方面都是一个单人协调职能的人。黄仁勋每年都会发表多次主题演讲，他将其解释为他如何与生态系统进行广泛的沟通，并以在亚洲特别是吃喝玩乐而闻名，他让不情愿的供应商相信人工智能繁荣是真实的，并为英伟达锁定了其产出的最大份额及其对年度发布周期的惊人承诺。
黄在相对默默无闻的情况下工作了数十年，主要为游戏玩家所知，在科技行业也几乎不为人知，但现在他成为了摇滚明星，无论走到哪里，总是穿着黑色皮夹克。他还成为了一名政治人物，这对他来说最终是不利的。英伟达长期以来在华盛顿特区或北京都没有业务，并因拜登政府在 2022 年实施芯片控制而措手不及。英伟达对这些最初的控制措施（基于互连速度限制出口）的立即反应是立即在中国发布 A800，这是一款 A100，其三分之一的互连被禁用。这为冲突定下了基调，我认为这是黄仁勋垮台的真正原因：黄仁勋极力反对芯片禁令的各种迭代，而英伟达只是费心做最低限度的事情来遵守规则。

【原文 English Original】
Listen to this post: Dearly beloved, we are gathered here today to get through this thing called life. ―  Prince Jensen Huang, CEO of Nvidia, 1993–2026 Jensen Huang resigned as CEO of Nvidia on Thursday, November 12, 2026. He had been CEO of the company ever since he founded it on April 5, 1993. Nvidia started out as a graphics card company; Huang’s exit — nominally because of affairs with a buyer who may or may not have been a Chinese spy, as well as at least two company employees — was ultimately because Nvidia was, by the powers that be, considered a defense contractor, and Huang never adjusted. In this, Huang was the ultimate victim of his own success. Nvidia’s first graphics cards simply translated triangles into pixels. The 2001 GeForce 3 introduced a programmable pixel shader, which meant a video card’s functionality was no longer pre-defined. The killer move, however — which almost killed the company — was the 2006 introduction of CUDA, which was an API for programming those shaders. For much of the next 16 years Huang sold the gospel of CUDA , convinced it was the platform for a future of accelerated computing; then, in 2022, came ChatGPT. ChatGPT made clear what GPUs were most useful for: large language models, and Nvidia made the best GPUs. More than that, Huang had realized that the future of accelerated computing was not just chips, but rather systems; that drove the purchase of Mellanox in 2019, which provided the technology for Nvidia to scale out from chips, setting it down the road to being the best option for the sort of large scale training that made large language models possible. For this Nvidia charged very high prices, with margins exceeding 70%, because they could: they had the platform, the technology, and, over the past few years as others sought to make their own chips, the supply chain. Huang’s impact on the Asian supply chain in particular cannot be overstated. Byrne Hobart, in his book Boom: Bubbles and the End of Stagnation , notes that one of the benefits of bubbles is that they provide a coordination function, as the fear of missing out incentivizes multiple entities with interlocking dependencies to all commit to building at the same time; Huang was, in many respects, a one-person coordination function. Huang gave multiple keynotes a year, which he explained as how he communicated with the ecosystem broadly, and was famous for eating and drinking his way across Asia in particular, convincing reluctant suppliers that the AI boom was real, and locking up the lion’s share of their output for Nvidia and its stunning commitment to a yearly release cycle. Huang, who had toiled for decades in relative obscurity, known primarily to gamers, and only barely to the tech industry, became a rock star, swarmed wherever he went, always in his black leather jacket. He also, to his ultimate detriment, became a political figure. Nvidia had long had no presence in either Washington D.C. or Beijing , and was blindsided by the Biden administration’s imposition of chip controls in 2022. Nvidia’s immediate reaction to those initial controls, which restricted exports based on interconnect speed, was to immediately release the A800 in China, which was an A100 with a third of its interconnects disabled. That set the tone for the conflict that I believe was the true cause of Huang’s downfall: Huang strenuously disagreed with the various iterations of the chip ban, and Nvidia only bothered to do the bare minimum to abide by the letter of the law, never the spirit. That approach, in all likelihood, extended to Nvidia’s oversight (or lack thereof) of Singaporean entities that were alleged to be fronts for chips for China. Some of these were legal: Chinese companies are allowed to access cloud computing facilities outside of China that house leading edge Nvidia chips, although chip control advocates are seeking to close that loophole; some were not legal, in that the chips were ultimately ferried to China. Megaspeed, whose executive, Alice Huang, was the first person Huang was alleged to have an affair with, was officially in the former business, and alleged to actually be in the latter. There are whispers that Megaspeed’s ultimate customer was not, or not just, Alibaba, but also the Chinese military. These are whispers, to be clear; it was the affairs that were enough, at least publicly, to lead to Huang’s resignation. Nvidia, Most Valuable Company in the World, 2024–2026 Nvidia’s durability — at least that of their margins — was already an open question. Start with CUDA: when the market was software written for GPUs, a platform — including not just an API but a huge set of libraries targeting every conceivable market for accelerated computing — was a nearly impenetrable moat. That is why LLMs like GPT were written using CUDA. LLMs, though, both brought Nvidia its incredible success, and also seeded its greatest risks. The first is that the vast majority of developer energy moved up the stack, using the LLM’s API as a platform; for most companies, CUDA didn’t matter. The second is that Anthropic, which found funding from Amazon and Google, originally also-rans to the Microsoft-OpenAI partnership, had to learn how to use Trainium chips from Amazon and TPUs from Google; this was difficult, but ultimately meant that the leading LLM did not have any Nvidia dependency at all (Anthropic runs on Nvidia chips, because they learned how to run on anything). The third is the most devastating: LLMs are so effective at writing software that any software-based moat will inevitably dry up. Nvidia’s second moat, its networking and systems approach, is more durable, although challenged by Google (and by extension, Anthropic) in particular. Nvidia’s systems approach is also the easy answer for enterprises and governments seeking to own their own hardware, and neoclouds seeking to build data centers that are independent of the hyperscalers. The latter market rents chips to both hyperscalers and frontier labs, as well as individual companies, but is challenged as obvious sources of power and political permission disappear. They also need money to afford Nvidia’s systems, which has increasingly come from Nvidia itself. Nvidia’s third moat is its mastery of the supply chain, and this is the moat that suddenly looks much more tenuous. Huang has bragged about the fact that he has never signed a contract with TSMC over their three decades of partnership; it’s a relationship built on a handshake and mutual trust with Huang specifically. This is, per the point above, a very Asian way of doing business, and Huang was the master of that. It’s questionable whether or not that trust and willingness to commit will persist when the handshake is no longer there. Nvidia’s most important moat, however, was the degree to which it was not a normal company. Huang organized Nvidia as an exoskeleton around one man: himself. There is very little management at Nvidia — Huang famously has 60 direct reports — for the same reason that there was no succession plan: Nvidia could move so quickly and so aggressively because the company still behaved as if it were a startup. Indeed, lots of established companies — including those still led by founders — claim to still be a startup, but only one, Nvidia, really was organized that way. That paid off with all of those successful bets; it also created an environment where there were no checks on Huang. And, now that he is gone, the exoskeleton is much more poised to collapse than you might expect. The AI Bubble, 2025–2027? The first part of the AI buildout was funded by free cash flow, particularly from the hyperscalers. Then, during the second half of last year, nearly everyone started turning to debt. Now — starting with Google this past summer — the primary funding mechanism is equity. In the long run, this should come full circle, and future build-outs will once again be funded by free cash flow, generated from the infrastructure that is being built now. The problem for Nvidia is that the companies most able to navigate this progression are the hyperscalers, which have the resources to challenge Nvidia’s hold on the chip market. To that end, Nvidia has been very eager to ensure that it is selling not only to the hyperscalers, but to other would-be competitors, like the neoclouds; there will likely, at some point, be serious questions raised about exactly how Nvidia went about allocating compute in pursuit of this goal. The neoclouds, however, are at a meaningful disadvantage when it comes to funding. First, their debt is significantly more expensive, given that their only business is renting GPUs (as opposed to, say, running the most valuable advertising businesses in the world, or the world’s largest e-commerce platform, or dominating enterprise software). Second, their equity is increasingly worthless, given the significant risks attached to that credit. If a neocloud can’t pay, it’s the equity holders that get wiped out first. This led to what I termed Nvidia’s Risky Business : Nvidia increasingly used its cash flow and credit rating to backstop and fund the companies who were buying its chips. Bears called this circular financing; bulls called it a necessary bridge to a future where AI revenue paid down these companies’ debt and drove massive upside. What is undoubtedly true is that this was the sort of risky business that is uniquely possible for a multi-trillion dollar company that is completely controlled by one man, who has made an entire career of pushing the limits and making risky bets — and seeing them pay off. It’s also a series of bets that are unlikely to continue. The neoclouds should be very nervous about losing their patron, along with their creditors and equity holders. The other problem is that the revenue necessary to make all of this build-out work is something on the order of a trillion dollars industry-wide, and it needs to materialize sooner rather than later; if it falls short, it’s the hyperscalers who will prioritize their own compute first, and they will likely be seen as a safe haven for everyone committing to spending. In that world, Nvidia’s neocloud hedge — absent Huang’s willingness to shore the ecosystem up — is liable to turn into a millstone, with their assets flooding the market even as the supply chain ramp-up brings ever more supply to market. AI as Normal Technology and the U.S. Semiconductor Industry, 1947~2047 Perhaps because he had been preaching the gospel of accelerated computing for so long, Huang was the leading figure pushing back against the doomer narrative surrounding AI. Yes, AI was a massive business opportunity, but it was still normal technology; the safety issues presented were engineering challenges to be solved. What required consideration was not just the next five years, but the next fifty. It’s a view that I am, in full disclosure, generally aligned with. Many others are not. On one hand there are the aforementioned doomers, certain that fast takeoff is imminent — or has already started — as AI increasingly builds better AI in a recursive loop. The end state is an AI that is massively more capable than humans, and uncontrollable by them; the only hope is to ensure that AI is aligned with humanity, by which adherents to this viewpoint mean aligned with them and their view of the world. This contingent is, broadly speaking, represented by Anthropic. And, in this view, actively working to enable and accelerate uncontrollable open weights models is a threat to humanity. On the other hand there are the China hawks, who view AI as a national security issue, and the key to U.S. military dominance in a world where China owns the means of production of most militarily relevant hardware. In this world giving China access to chips is effectively treason against the United States. For both of these groups, Huang was public enemy number one, because of his determination to do what was best for Nvidia’s business, which was to sell chips to China. This made sense for Nvidia for multiple reasons: The first and most obvious reason is that it is good for a company to be able to sell to everyone, including the second largest market in the world (China has traditionally made up about a quarter of Nvidia’s sales, long before AI was even a thing). The second is that China is a large enough market, with sufficiently motivated and capable developers, that it can actually create a meaningful CUDA alternative; furthermore, such an alternative would, in the long run, not be constrained to China, but rather compete with Nvidia all over the world. The third is that China’s AI ecosystem, unconstrained as it is by such niceties as terms of service, distills frontier lab models and releases them as open weights models; those models, meanwhile, are tuned to run on Nvidia chips. These models give Nvidia leverage versus the frontier labs all over the world, including in the West. The fourth is that China is uniquely positioned to create a fundamentally different approach to systems design using optical interconnects to scale out training clusters. This is much more inefficient in terms of power usage than Nvidia’s more elegant designs, but China is also much more capable of manufacturing excess amounts of power to make it work. The fifth is that, in the very long run, China can create an entire alternative supply chain for semiconductors broadly, rendering Nvidia’s mastery of the Western-aligned supply chain much less important. This last point is worth dwelling on. The chief objection that China hawks in particular make to the idea that it is a good idea to sell China chips in order to prevent them from surpassing the U.S. is that China is already heavily invested in building their own ecosystem. This is certainly true, but I think it underplays the complexity of chips and what is necessary to actually compete with the West. Specifically, the Chinese government can only control the supply side, by spending money and making top-down imperatives; building an ecosystem, however, whether that be for AI specifically, or semiconductors broadly, requires demand as well. Progress in models and systems and chips depends on a feedback loop between the user and the developer, or the customer and the manufacturer. The demand side, however, is much more short-term oriented than the Chinese government might prefer. The model companies’ concern is the other model companies: that means if they are distilling, we must distill too. If they are using Nvidia chips, then we must too. This matters up and down the stack, just as it has always mattered in technology, which really is different in this regard from almost every other industry. A useful analogy is to consider the Internet. Why is it that country after country can profess a desire to have an indigenous alternative to the American tech giants, yet miserably fail in every attempt to generate it? It’s because the tech giants are only a click away! In this regard, China’s Great Firewall was one of the most brilliant geostrategic moves ever: by virtue of cutting off access to the American tech companies, China created the demand that pulled China’s own tech giants into existence. You need demand, not just desire. This is why China itself is currently banning the import of Nvidia’s two-generations-behind H20 chips, after the Trump administration foolishly banned their import, only to reverse themselves while bragging about the reason to do so — i.e. keep China addicted to Nvidia. China is replaying the Great Firewall playbook: force its internal demand to use its much worse alternatives, because that is the only way those alternatives become better. And, in the long run, those alternatives, and the entire ecosystem that supports them, will flood the world. Huang was, to be perfectly clear, talking his book when it came to his insistence on selling chips to China, or, in the case of the current controversy, allegedly turning a blind eye towards nominally legal buyers who were intent on violating the chip ban; that doesn’t mean, however, that he was wrong about the long-term effects, at least if AI is a normal technology (and I haven’t gotten to the risks this imposes on the Taiwan Strait ). What is clear now, however, is that the doomers and the hawks have won: AI, at least in terms of policy, will be treated as anything but normal, and in the fullness of time, it is the U.S. chip ecosystem that will pay the ultimate price. Tech Company Independence, 1968–2026 The birth date for the last obituary was the invention of the transistor; the birth date for this one is the founding of Intel. Robert Noyce and co-founders had spent the last decade at Fairchild Semiconductor, but were constrained by their parent company’s fundamental conservatism and chafed at their lack of upside. Arthur Rock effectively created the venture capital industry in Silicon Valley through his financing of Intel; Noyce created the concept of the commercial-market-led technology company that made it up in volume. At that time the largest single purchaser of chips was the U.S. government; Noyce realized that the fastest way to progress was to make chips for everyone, including the government, and on his terms, not theirs. From that point on, tech as an industry operated with the assumption that the world was its customer, and that their own executives defined the route to progress. Government was free to buy their products, but not to define them, and if they wanted the best products, then they best not restrict who they could sell them to either. That’s how important volume was, and, over time, it became clear how powerful and essential ecosystems were. Other industries operate differently; I thought this article in the Financial Times was striking, and not just because of the headline: Bessent says Nvidia needs ‘shake-up’ with external CEO : Bessent said that it is important “to examine whether Nvidia had a culture of compliance around the US export restrictions” and whether its top executives knew they were being skirted. “Was it a low-level fail? Was it in the middle, or was it up in the C-suite? And who knew? These shell companies were obvious, they were being investigated, and did Nvidia use them as a workaround to sell chips to the Chinese?” he said. “Were they pressing these seemingly illicit sales to goose their revenues and their earnings?” The Treasury secretary added that Nvidia needs to provide answers within a matter of days: “I think we need answers in the next 10 days from the board and from the outside counsel”. He added that “we will see if Nvidia intentionally ignored the warning signs of these shell companies, many of them in Singapore”. Bessent has pointed the spotlight on Howard Lutnick’s commerce department for failing to ban exports of Nvidia’s chips to Megaspeed, the Singaporean company linked to the alleged Chinese spy who had an affair with Huang. US authorities have been investigating whether Megaspeed, which builds AI data centres in Asia, has been involved in smuggling high-end Nvidia chips, which are powering the AI boom, into China. Bessent has blamed the commerce department more than once this week for failing to ban exports of Nvidia’s chips to Megaspeed. Commerce delayed efforts to add Megaspeed to Washington’s blacklist of companies the US considers a risk to national security. “Many other departments were pushing for this, and commerce had the pen,” Bessent repeated on Sunday. “We have all the rules we need. We just need them enforced.” Lutnick is under mounting pressure from within the administration and from Congress, which has demanded that he explain how he allowed chips to be exported to a company linked to an alleged Chinese spy. US lawmakers are also accelerating efforts to crack down on advanced AI chips reaching China. If Nvidia “were a bank and they hadn’t complied like this, the [Treasury’s Office of the Comptroller of the Currency] would be in there right now, and a lot of the executives would be removed”, Bessent said. Scott Bessent is the Treasury Secretary, which is to say that he operates an apparatus that is arguably just as, if not more, powerful than the U.S. military. Treasury controls the flow of money around the world, and its soldiers are the banks; if Treasury has sanctioned an entity, then it is up to banks to ensure those sanctions are enforced. They need to know their customers, and they need to analyze every dollar flowing through their systems; if they do not, they are breaking the law. Ignorance is not a defense. Ignorance, on the other hand, has been tech’s defense basically forever. Yes, there are bad people in the world, which means that if the whole world is using your products, they will be used to do bad things. That was considered an acceptable trade-off, however, because most people are good and the benefits that come from scale — and an avoidance of the friction that comes from trying to track the activities of billions of people — were worth the risk. This was certainly what Huang believed, and, to his detriment, he aggressively belittled anyone who dared disagree (the extent to which Huang is despised in Washington D.C., as evidenced by the giddiness and bloodlust online last week, is extraordinary). In Huang’s view, as long as the Commerce Department said that it was ok to sell to Megaspeed, then it was ok to sell to Megaspeed — and to sleep with one of its executives. Bessent views the matter entirely differently: he thinks that Nvidia should operate like a bank. It’s not just their job to abide by the letter of the law, but the spirit of it. It’s not the government’s job to enforce the chip ban, but the company’s. An attestation from a Singaporean customer that chips aren’t going to China isn’t worth anything; actually putting boots on the ground and ensuring compliance is the only way Nvidia cannot be in violation of the U.S. government’s dictates. Again, for tech, this is extraordinary, even if it is normal in banking. Extraordinary enough, in fact, that Huang is being labeled by many — not just in Washington, but also in the finance world — as a traitor. Huang, in my estimation, is just a businessman who cares about nothing else other than Nvidia; that worked out great when he made GPUs for gaming that no one in government cared about or understood. That’s just a normal technology; when AI was deemed to be anything but normal, however, business as usual wasn’t just over: it was a crime, and it cost Huang his job — and maybe more. It’s worth pointing out that while this episode was shocking, I should not, in retrospect, have been surprised. Earlier this year, when Anthropic faced off against the U.S. government, I wrote in Anthropic and Alignment : At the same time, what is the standard by which it should be decided what is allowed and not allowed if not laws, which are passed by an elected Congress? Anthropic’s position is that Amodei — who I am using as a stand-in for Anthropic’s management and its board — ought to decide what its models are used for, despite the fact that Amodei is not elected and not accountable to the public. And, on the second point, who decides when and in what way American military capabilities are used? That is the responsibility of the Department of War, which ultimately answers to the President, who also is elected. Once again, however, Anthropic’s position is that an unaccountable Amodei can unilaterally restrict what its models are used for. My point in that Article was that if AI is as exceptional as claimed, then the government will demand a say in how it is used, whether or not private company executives agree; moreover, that was a good thing, or at least a least-bad thing. The same analysis applies to Nvidia and Huang: Huang may have fundamentally disagreed with the chip ban, but at the end of the day, it was his duty to accept that it was the law of the land. To the extent he did not do so is ultimately his responsibility. American Exceptionalism, 1776–2026 Perhaps the most tragic aspect of the Huang affair is the extent to which he was the personification of The American Dream. Huang was sent to America as a nine year old who didn’t speak a lick of English, and somehow ended up at a boarding school in rural Kentucky for misbehaving youth, where he would trade help on homework for protection from bullies. From there he went to a state school in Oregon, became an engineer, before famously ending up at a Denny’s diner where he and his co-founders decided to start Nvidia. Then, over the following 33 years, he took risk after risk, created innovation after innovation, until he became a hero not just in the United States, but across the world. And then, you might say, he flew too close to the sun. Certainly he did so in his private life: it’s not just the affairs, which may be par for the course for rich and powerful men; rather, it’s notable just how reckless the affairs were. The ones that were revealed last week were with a customer and potential Chinese spy, and two of his own employees; both are fireable offenses. Meanwhile, the way in which Huang treated his opponents — including actively seeking to get people fired who he felt stood in the way of getting his way — bore the marks of a man who has constructed a life, and a company, where no one can or will stand up to him. That is a recipe for disaster, and here we are. At the same time, it really does bum me out that what ultimately doomed Huang was a set of rules that really are a big departure from the status quo — and, in my opinion, misguided. Huang’s actions — or lack of actions, in terms of enforcing compliance with the chip ban — are treated as if they are an obvious crime, when in fact this is a dramatic shift in expectations from a short time ago (although there is certainly a callback to previous controversies around selling advanced computing to adversaries). Huang should have adjusted and accepted the new reality, make no mistake; I’m sympathetic to the fact he couldn’t, and recognize the failure in not having structures in place that could have warned him about the dangerous road he was embarking on, even as I realize Huang’s willingness to navigate dangerous roads is precisely why he was an American success story. Beyond Huang, however, there is the question of how we compete with China, and I am disappointed, although not surprised, that we are pursuing the route of bans and forced compliance, instead of innovation and openness. Make no mistake, I am no China dove, and I have been very early to the argument that we erred greatly in willingly exporting entire industries to the communist state. That, however, makes it even more imperative that we sprint in the opposite direction of China, towards more freedom in a bet on inventing new industries, not more control and a focus on gatekeeping what we have. I get the logic, particularly in the case of AI, which is extraordinary; I lament the implications of what it says about our belief in ourselves and our ability to stay ahead. Presented by As AI models improve, you might expect the market will consolidate around a handful of providers. But user data tells a different story. Among OpenRouter customers spending at least $100 a month, the median number of AI model families in use has doubled over the past year , from three to six. Even as AI models become more capable, businesses are using more models, not fewer. This makes sense when you consider that intelligence isn’t one-dimensional. A model that’s exceptional at writing code may not be the fastest at answering customer questions, or the most economical at processing millions of documents. The question is shifting from “which AI model should we build on?” to “which model should handle each task?” The answer, increasingly, is ‘it depends.’ Which is great for flexibility, less great for simplicity. OpenRouter, which recently joined Stripe , allows businesses to access and govern hundreds of models with the flexibility to optimize for cost, performance, and reliability as the market evolves. Learn more at openrouter.ai .

Why Is Beijing So Determined to Pursue Reunification With Taiwan? – The Diplomat

Taiwan is widely seen as one of the world’s major potential flashpoints. Particularly since Russia’s invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, concerns have grown among observers, analysts, and policymakers in the United States, other Western countries, and the Asia-Pacific region that Beijing may take military action against Taiwan, which Beijing perceives as moving increasingly toward independence under the Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) government. Xi Jinping’s increasingly assertive pursuit of cross-strait reunification has further intensified these concerns.
Why is Beijing so determined to achieve reunification with Taiwan? Despite extensive discussions in the media, academia, and policy circles outside mainland China, this question has yet to receive a sufficiently convincing answer.
A prevailing view outside China emphasizes the significant strategic and security advantages that cross-strait reunification would bring to Beijing. According to this perspective, reunification with Taiwan would enable Beijing to break through the security constraints imposed by the U.S. and its allies and extend China’s maritime defense perimeter outward. This would not only substantially strengthen Beijing’s strategic position in the Asia-Pacific region but also enhance the People’s Liberation Army’s (PLA) ability to project military power beyond the First Island Chain. This interpretation of Beijing’s motivation for reunification also reflects Washington’s and its regional allies’ concerns about the strategic implications of China’s control over Taiwan.
Another important motivation frequently attributed to Beijing by U.S. analysts and policymakers in recent years is the prospect of gaining control over Taiwan’s advanced semiconductor industry, particularly its leading-edge chip manufacturing capabilities, which occupy a critical position in the global semiconductor supply chain and the ongoing China-U.S. technological competition.
If these are indeed Beijing’s two primary motivations for pursuing cross-strait reunification, then, given Taiwan’s strong resistance to political incorporation under Chinese Communist Party (CCP) rule, Beijing could fully realize these two objectives only by establishing direct control over the island, most plausibly through a successful military invasion. Moreover, to achieve the objective of controlling Taiwan’s semiconductor industry, the island’s manufacturing capabilities would need to remain intact and operational following a successful invasion by the PLA.
Nevertheless, whether Beijing will ultimately resort to military force to reunify Taiwan remains uncertain, as does the question of whether such an invasion, if undertaken, would succeed. In the view of John Lee and Jan-Peter Kleinhans, “invasion likely remains at the bottom of the list for China’s leaders when sizing up solutions to the ‘Taiwan problem.’” If the use of force to reunify Taiwan is not a foregone conclusion, the only other option for Beijing to achieve both objectives would be peaceful reunification, requiring Taiwan to agree voluntarily to political incorporation into the People’s Republic of China (PRC) under CCP rule. Yet such a scenario appears highly implausible given the Taiwanese people’s strong sense of Taiwanese identity and deep-seated resentment against Beijing’s communist regime and authoritarian system.
Furthermore, historical evidence also calls these material-interest explanations into question. As late as 2001, then-Chinese leader Jiang Zemin explicitly indicated that, following reunification, Taiwan could retain its own political and economic systems and armed forces and administer its domestic affairs without the deployment of PLA troops or mainland administrative personnel on the island. Jiang’s statement suggests that direct strategic and military control over Taiwan was not an indispensable objective of Beijing’s reunification policy.
Against this background, it is difficult to argue convincingly that Beijing’s determined pursuit of reunification with Taiwan is primarily motivated by the prospect of improving its strategic and security position and gaining control over Taiwan’s semiconductor industry. These are undoubtedly two advantages that reunification through a successful military invasion could potentially bring to Beijing, but they don’t seem to be the main rationale for this strategic goal. What, then, is the primary motivation behind Beijing’s determined pursuit of reunification with Taiwan in recent years, particularly under Xi Jinping?
A closer examination of Beijing’s Taiwan policy reveals that, fundamentally, the CCP views reunification with Taiwan as a nationalist issue rather than one driven primarily by material interests. In other words, cross-strait reunification is regarded first and foremost as an issue of deep national sentiment, emotion, and pride.
During his interview with CBS journalist Mike Wallace on September 2, 1986, Deng Xiaoping made this point explicit. In response to Wallace’s question, “What’s in it for Taiwan to be reunified with the mainland?” Deng explained: “First of all, it is a national question, a question of national sentiments. All members of the Chinese nation want to see China reunified. The present state of division is contrary to our national will.”
For Beijing, Taiwan embodies the Chinese people’s painful historical memories and symbolizes the nation’s “century of humiliation” stemming from the encroachment of Western and Japanese colonial powers on a weak China from the 19th century through the first half of the 20th century. Consequently, cross-strait reunification is regarded as an indispensable step toward overcoming this national trauma and an integral part of the nationalist mission of achieving the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation by the mid-21st century. It is within this nationalist context that Beijing has consistently identified Taiwan as a “core interest” – a foreign policy principle that cannot be compromised.
In a further analysis, however, reunification with Taiwan, along with other core interests identified by the CCP leadership – including state sovereignty, territorial integrity, national security, and economic development and modernization – is subordinate to Beijing’s paramount core interest of preserving China’s existing political system, namely, the CCP’s monopoly on the nation’s political power. In other words, all other core interests ultimately serve to advance the paramount core interest of the security and preservation of the communist regime. Both Beijing’s domestic and foreign policies are fundamentally formulated to ensure regime security.
Cross-strait reunification, as a core national interest, is always used by the CCP first and foremost as an important means of enhancing the legitimacy and security of the communist regime. The other potential material benefits of reunification – such as overcoming the security constraints of the First Island Chain, extending the country’s maritime defense perimeter outward, and gaining access to Taiwan’s advanced semiconductor capabilities – are only secondary to this fundamental objective of regime security.
Particularly as China’s economic growth has slowed significantly in recent years, Beijing can no longer rely on rapid economic growth as a source of regime legitimacy to the extent that it did for nearly four decades following the launch of economic reforms in the late 1970s. Consequently, Xi now places even greater emphasis on reunification as a means of sustaining regime legitimacy and security through nationalist mobilization, particularly in the context of mounting domestic economic and social difficulties.
Along this line of thinking, it can be inferred that cross-strait reunification is pursued by Beijing to strengthen the Chinese communist regime. Thus, although Beijing appears offensive on the surface in pushing hard for a “one country, two systems” reunification, the CCP’s proposed model of reunification is fundamentally defensive in nature. Given the paramount objective of maintaining and enhancing regime legitimacy and security, Xi’s “one country, two systems” scheme is designed, on the one hand, to enhance the legitimacy of the CCP regime through reunification with Taiwan and, on the other hand, to use “two systems” as a political firewall to protect the communist regime from the potentially subversive influence of Taiwan’s democracy.
Ironically, if Taipei were to shift its policy from resisting Xi’s “one country, two systems” reunification proposal to advocating reunification under a democratic political system grounded in Sun Yat-sen’s Three Principles of the People, Beijing would find itself in a political dilemma. In his November 12, 2026 speech at a gathering commemorating the 160th anniversary of Sun Yat-sen’s birth, Xi Jinping called for carrying forward Sun Yat-sen’s legacy and achieving complete national reunification as an integral part of the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Yet would Beijing actually accept cross-strait reunification under a democratic political system based on Sun’s Three Principles of the People if such reunification were to jeopardize the CCP’s one-party rule?
This underlying political logic of the Taiwan issue appears to have received little attention from policymakers and analysts in both Washington and Taipei.

content:
Megaspeed位于新加坡的办公室。该公司表示，前高管黄乐目前在公司没有担任任何职务。美国官员指控她为中国从事间谍活动。 Taryn Ng/Agence France-Presse — Getty Images
新加坡数据中心公司Megaspeed周日发表声明称，前高管黄乐已于2025年8月离职。黄乐是美国官员所称的一起针对英伟达联合创始人黄仁勋的中国间谍阴谋的核心人物。
据美联社报道，这是自黄乐因与黄仁勋的关系受到国际社会密切关注以来，Megaspeed首次直接回应她在公司的任职情况。黄仁勋已于周四从英伟达辞职。
两人关系的曝光震动了英伟达这家人工智能芯片领域的主导企业，也波及全球科技行业和美国政府。
上个月，《纽约时报》报道称，美国官员已认定黄乐是中国情报机构的一名情报人员，并与黄仁勋关系密切。黄仁勋是人工智能热潮中最有影响力的人物之一，也是特朗普总统的顾问。
上周日，黄仁勋承认自己曾与黄乐有过婚外情，英伟达董事会则表示，已开始调查他的行为。周三，《纽约时报》报道称，他还与一名直接向他汇报工作的英伟达高管有婚外情。第二天，他突然辞去了这家由自己领导了30多年的公司的首席执行官职务。
这家芯片制造商的股价已较一个多月前创下的历史高点下跌约30%，市值蒸发超过1万亿美元。
这场丑闻也使Megaspeed受到关注。这家规模不大的公司在2024年至2026年间购买了价值数十亿美元的英伟达芯片，而这些芯片在市场上一直供不应求。
这引发了美国商务部的一项调查，以确定部分芯片是否被转运至中国，从而可能违反美国的出口限制。美国尚未对该公司提出任何正式指控。
周四，Megaspeed首席执行官詹姆斯·陈(James Tan)在一份声明中表示，公司没有违反美国法律，已配合商务部调查人员，并“准备与美国政府任何其他相关部门全面合作”。
Megaspeed周日的声明重申，公司业务“正当合法”，并首次提及黄乐。黄乐从2023年起参与筹建该公司。声明称，她目前已不在公司担任任何职务。
“Megaspeed不对黄女士的个人及私事发表评论，”该公司在发给美联社的电子邮件声明中表示。
Megaspeed提供的有关黄乐任职时间的信息尚无法得到独立核实。周日发表这份声明之前，美国和新加坡当局已对该公司进行了长达一年多的审查。
“公司已聘请外部法律顾问进行彻底的内部调查，”Megaspeed还表示。
黄乐尚未回应置评请求。中国否认了有关间谍活动的指控。
《纽约时报》曾于2025年10月援引一名人力资源经理的说法报道，黄乐已在数月前离开该公司，但当时不清楚她去了哪里。
上周，新加坡政府表示，由于黄乐在Megaspeed的相关事务中“可能作出虚假申报”，当局曾于2025年6月至2026年2月期间扣押她的护照。她最终获释，但被禁止再次入境新加坡。
包括国务卿马可·鲁比奥在内的美国官员，早在2025年10月就已向特朗普通报了对黄乐及其与黄仁勋关系的担忧。
特朗普没有采取行动。今年5月，特朗普还带着黄仁勋一同访问中国。这再次表明，黄仁勋对于人工智能数据中心建设热潮的重要性，而这股热潮正是美国经济增长的关键驱动力之一。
这场丑闻引发了特朗普政府内部围绕人工智能及对华政策的新一轮内斗。
商务部长霍华德·卢特尼克一直积极主张允许英伟达等美国企业向亚洲销售产品。如今，政府内部其他官员和国会议员指责他领导的商务部与英伟达及黄仁勋的关系过于密切。
财长斯科特·贝森特周五表示，财政部和其他部门支持将Megaspeed列入贸易黑名单，但只有商务部才有权采取这一步骤。商务部表示，此类决定需要整个政府共同作出。
贝森特周日表示，英伟达应该从公司外部寻找新任首席执行官。他在福克斯新闻的《周日早间期货》节目中说，该公司需要“一场大刀阔斧的变革”。
他还表示，英伟达董事会及外部法律顾问必须在未来10天内，就公司遵守出口管制规定的合规文化回应外界的质疑。

content:
资料照片：美国总统唐纳德·特朗普登上空军一号专机。(2026年6月17日)
美国总统唐纳德·特朗普(Donald Trump)星期一(11月16日)将启程前往菲律宾马尼拉，与参加东盟峰会的东南亚国家领导人会晤，出席东盟-美国特别峰会(ASEAN-US Special Summit)，并与东道国菲律宾总统小费迪南德·马科斯(Ferdinand Marcos Jr.)举行会谈。
据菲律宾官方通讯社PNA报道，特朗普总统将于当地时间星期二下午5点30分抵达马尼拉，东盟会议预计在当晚6点结束。PNA报道，特朗普总统将出席星期二在帕塞市(Pasay City)菲律宾国际会议中心举行的东盟-美国特别峰会。
白宫助理新闻秘书奥利维亚·韦尔斯(Olivia Wales)上周五表示，特朗普将对菲律宾首都马尼拉展开为期两天的访问，进行一系列会议，旨在“巩固美国在自由开放的印太地区的领导地位”。
东盟2026年发言人多米尼克·哈维尔·英佩里尔(Dominic Xavier Imperial)表示，菲律宾总统马科斯将在星期二东盟峰会最后一天，主持第29届东盟加三峰会和第21届东亚峰会，然后召开东盟-美国特别峰会。
英佩里尔表示，在东盟-美国特别峰会上，各国领导人预计会更开放地讨论地缘政治变化如何影响该地区。他还表示，东盟预计将与华盛顿达成至少两份文件：一份涵盖政治安全、经济和贸易关系，另一份涉及网络诈骗和跨国犯罪。
今年6月，美国与东盟在印尼雅加达举行了第38届年度美国-东盟对话(U.S.-ASEAN Dialogue)，强调在美国-东盟全面战略伙伴关系(U.S.-ASEAN Comprehensive Strategic Partnership)下正在开展强有力的合作，以推进共同的经济及安全目标，建设一个自由开放的印太地区。
美国智库外交关系委员会(Council on Foreign Relations)星期天发表报告指出，在美国国会中期选举后，部分亚洲国家领导人正在关注选举结果是否可能促使白宫的亚洲政策发生变化，东盟-美国特别峰会将是这些领导人观察美国亚洲政策的一个机会。
报告也预计，特朗普可能推动东南亚国家加入美国主导的“硅和平”(Pax Silica)倡议，并鼓励各国采用美国的超级智能(通常称人工智能或AI)技术体系；美国也可能宣布与越南、泰国达成贸易框架。不过，报告指出，中国超级智能模型价格较低、正在吸引用户，这些因素有可能限制美国的成果。
与此同时，东盟发言人英佩里尔证实，马科斯将在特朗普访问菲律宾的短暂期间与其举行双边会谈。
特朗普上一次以总统身份访问菲律宾是在2017年他的第一个任期内，当时他出席了在马尼拉举行的美国-东盟峰会，并与时任菲律宾总统杜特尔特会晤。
菲律宾是美国的正式条约盟友，今年也适逢《美菲共同防御条约》签署75周年。有分析认为，特朗普选择先在马尼拉参加东盟峰会，再赴中国参加亚太经合组织(APEC)峰会，让这趟亚洲行包含东盟外交与美菲关系议程，向菲律宾和东南亚传递了重要信息，显示华盛顿仍积极参与东南亚事务，并在特朗普与习近平会面前重申对菲律宾及地区伙伴的关注。
对马科斯来说，与特朗普的会谈提供了一个机会，可以在南中国海紧张局势加剧的情况下，强化华盛顿对菲律宾的承诺，同时推动防务合作和经济联系。
外交关系委员会报告指出，特朗普与马科斯会谈的核心考验，是华盛顿能否给马尼拉更明确的安全支持。报告认为，特朗普可能给出概括性的保证，但不太可能承诺增加南中国海巡航或提供马尼拉所希望的军事援助。
由菲律宾主办的第49届东盟峰会星期天开幕，峰会汇聚东盟各国领导人及主要对话伙伴，包括澳大利亚、中国、印度、日本、韩国、联合国和美国。
星期天，东道主菲律宾外交部表示，东盟仍未能与中国就《南中国海行为准则》完成谈判，尽管双方已在大约80%的内容上达成了初步的共识。
“目前尚未达成最终结论，”菲律宾外交部长玛丽亚·特蕾莎·拉扎罗(Maria Theresa Daza-Lazaro)在东盟峰会期间举行的记者会上表示。
据菲律宾官员称，中国是由国务院总理李强代表出席马尼拉东盟峰会。李强星期一会晤东盟领导人，但在特朗普星期二抵达之前就会离开。
包括特朗普与马科斯在内的国家元首，将在星期三前往中国深圳出席亚太经合组织领导人非正式会议。

# 民主党高层指责商务部未能阻止中国取得先进芯片

美国参议院商务委员会首席民主党议员、华盛顿州联邦参议员坎特韦尔（Maria Cantwell）指控，商务部长卢特尼克（Howard Lutnick）多次收到联邦官员提出的国家安全警告，却未采取足够措施阻止受限制的美国先进AI芯片流入中国，可能危及美国的技术优势。她并质疑，卢特尼克的家族商业利益及政府出口收费政策，是否影响商务部决策。

发表时间： 16/11/2026 - 18:46

 10 分钟 浏览时间

 美国民主党女参议员Maria Cantwell Chip Somodevilla/Getty Images/AFP

 作者： [华盛顿特约记者 陈米亚](https://www.rfi.fr/cn/%E4%BD%9C%E8%80%85/%E9%99%88%E7%B1%B3%E4%BA%9A/ "华盛顿特约记者 陈米亚")

广告

继续浏览后续

坎特韦尔星期日致函卢特尼克，要求商务部加强出口管制，阻止被列入限制名单的企业取得美国敏感技术。她特别点名新加坡科技公司Megaspeed International，指商务部在多次收到国家安全警告后仍延误行动，甚至暂停相关调查，让该公司继续有机会取得先进AI芯片。

坎特韦尔在信中写道：“如果负责保护美国技术优势的政府机构，连自己的管制措施都无法执行，美国就不可能维持在人工智能领域的领导地位。”

她批评，商务部未能有效限制被视为国家安全风险的企业，削弱美国出口管制措施，让中国有机会利用美国敏感技术训练先进AI模型。她要求卢特尼克运用2018年《出口管制改革法》赋予商务部的权力，确保相关法律得到执行。

事件涉及Megaspeed前高层黄乐。美国情报官员怀疑她是中国间谍，并指该公司涉嫌协助中国取得受出口限制的美国芯片。美国《纽约时报》11月9日曾报道，商务部可能拖延对Megaspeed的调查。相关事件曝光之际，华盛顿传出黄乐曾与英伟达（Nvidia）前执行长黄仁勋有婚外情关系，引发政界关注。黄仁勋一直公开反对部分对华芯片出口限制，但目前没有资料证明他涉及相 关违法行为。

美国财政部长贝森特（Scott Bessent）也像美国财经新闻频道CNBC批评商务部处理事件的方式。他表示，财政部、国务院、国防部及美国贸易代表办公室数月前已支持将Megaspeed列入限制名单，但商务部一直未有配合。

贝森特说：“商务部掌握决定权，至于他们内部的处理程序，你们必须向他们查询。我的副手数月来一直在推动这件事。”

坎特韦尔也质疑卢特尼克可能涉及利益冲突。她指出，卢特尼克过去数十年领导的金融服务公司坎托菲茨杰拉德（Cantor Fitzgerald），目前由其儿子掌控。根据她在信中引用的资料，该公司在卢特尼克获提名出任商务部长时，持有价值约12亿美元的英伟达股票。

此外，特朗普政府对部分出口中国的英伟达芯片征收25%费用。坎特韦尔认为，这项政策可能令政府产生，透过批准敏感技术出口增加收入的诱因。她强调：“美国的国家安全和人工智能领导地位，不应受到家族商业利益影响，也不应因为一项透过出口关键技术，为联邦政府带来收入的政策，而受到损害。”

商务部截至星期一未有立即回应相关置评要求。

国会两党议员已开始要求政府交代事件。共和党籍南卡罗来纳州联邦参议员、参议院银行委员会主席斯科特（Tim Scott），星期四要求卢特尼克及黄仁勋于12月出席听证会。商务部发言人艾克哈默（Kristen Eichamer）上星期表示，卢特尼克已同意作证。

民主党参议员沃伦（Elizabeth Warren）及库恩斯（Chris Coons）上周也致函卢特尼克、国务卿鲁比奥（Marco Rubio）及白宫幕僚长史蒂芬米勒（Stephen Miller），要求保存所有涉及英伟达向中国出口先进AI芯片，以及可能转运相关芯片到中国的文件和通讯纪录，并要求三人于11月17日前确认已发出保存指示。

随着特朗普政府准备与中国领导层会面，芯片出口管制问题再受关注。卢特尼克预计本星期随特朗普前往中国，出席亚太经济合作组织（APEC）峰会相关活动。民主党预计明年1月起控制众议院及参议院，届时可能进一步调查英伟达出口及商务部的处理过程。

# 特朗普称或会向习近平提黄仁勋被针对的间谍指控：我不知道她是不是间谍

当被记者问到“您为什么不打算就针对黄仁勋和英伟达的间谍活动向习提出质问？”美国总统特朗普（Donald Trump）周一在白宫回答说：“我或许，我或许会谈的”。

发表时间： 16/11/2026 - 18:13 更改时间： 16/11/2026 - 18:26

 4 分钟 浏览时间

 11月16日，美国总统特朗普在白宫南草坪准备搭乘“海军陆战队一号”直升机离开前，与记者们交谈。 © 美联社图片

 作者： [弗林](https://www.rfi.fr/cn/%E4%BD%9C%E8%80%85/%E5%BC%97%E6%9E%97/ "弗林")

广告

继续浏览后续

当被问道“您是否相信美国情报的说法，即黄仁勋当时正在与一名中国间谍交往、存在婚外情？” 特朗普表示：“我并不确定她是不是中国间谍，我之前也这么说过。我当时上了史蒂芬·A·史密斯（Stephen A. Smith）的节目——他很棒。至于她到底是不是中国间谍，我还不清楚，我们会对此确定的”。

记者追问美国国务卿兼国家安全顾问卢比奥（Marco Rubio）：“曾告诉您，情报显示她是一名中国间谍；您相信该情报吗？” 特朗普反问道：“谁告诉我的？”

当记者提醒据报道是卢比奥时，特朗普说，“我没听说过，我没听说过，没有。我不知道她是不是间谍。通常这种情况是，只要有女性进入这个国家，尤其是来自中国的漂亮女人，人们就会说她是个间谍。我完全不知道她是不是间谍”。

当记者问“鉴于您与黄仁勋关系密切，且（他）被指与一名中国间谍有婚外情，对于那些担心国家安全因此受到威胁的美国人，您作何回应？”

特朗普回答称：“国家安全并未受到威胁，而且我们国家现在比以往任何时候都更加强大。你知道，中国会跟我们玩些手段，我们也会跟中国玩些手段”。特朗普续称，“我们的国家目前比以往任何时候都更加强大；无论在经济上还是军事上，我们都从未做到过这样的成就”。

特朗普告诉记者说：“黄仁勋显然面临两方面的情况，他有家庭方面的情况，这确实很棘手；而他真正想做的，是销售芯片”。特朗普还指出，美国政府已禁止英伟达向中国出售包括Blackwell在内的先进芯片。

title: 美前參議員：助中國加入世貿是悲劇性誤判
summary: 圖為美國前國際宗教自由大使、前參議員布朗巴克（Sam Brownback）資料照。（Samira Bouaou／大紀元） 【大紀元2026年11月17日訊】（大紀元記者李皓月編譯報導）亞太經濟合作組織（APEC）領導人非正式會議即將於11月18日至19日在中國深圳舉行，美中經貿關係及中國人權問題再度成為國際關注焦點。美國前參議員、前國際宗教自由大使薩姆‧布朗巴克（Sam Brownback）週一（11月16日）公開呼籲，「除非北京當局賦予人民宗教信仰自由，否則美國應終止與中國
content:
圖為美國前國際宗教自由大使、前參議員布朗巴克（Sam Brownback）資料照。（Samira Bouaou／大紀元）
【大紀元2026年11月17日訊】（大紀元記者李皓月編譯報導）亞太經濟合作組織（APEC）領導人非正式會議即將於11月18日至19日在中國深圳舉行，美中經貿關係及中國人權問題再度成為國際關注焦點。美國前參議員、前國際宗教自由大使薩姆‧布朗巴克（Sam Brownback）週一（11月16日）公開呼籲，「除非北京當局賦予人民宗教信仰自由，否則美國應終止與中國的永久正常貿易關係」。
布朗巴克在福克斯新聞發表評論文章，公開反思25年前支持中國加入全球貿易體系的決定。
他在文章中表示，2000年美國國會表決給予中國永久正常貿易關係（PNTR）地位時，他是投下贊成票的83名參議員之一。2001年，中國正式加入世界貿易組織（WTO），全面融入全球經濟。
布朗巴克坦言，這是自己14年參議員生涯中「投下的最糟糕的一票」。
布朗巴克指出，當年美國政策制定者以為，隨著中國融入全球經濟，中共政權將逐漸走向開放與自由。
然而，25年過去，中國經濟和軍事實力大幅增長，政治體制卻沒有朝民主化方向發展。他指控北京當局「惡意利用」其國際經貿地位，持續迫害維吾爾人、西藏人及法輪功修煉者，並對其實施種族滅絕，更是「組織了一個威權主義者聯盟來威脅自由世界，並助長了全球各地的人權侵害行為」。
他認為，美國當年允許中方加入世貿組織，實為一項「根本性政策錯誤」，事實證明是「悲劇性的誤判」（tragic miscalculation），並將當前美中關係形容為一場新的冷戰。
對此，布朗巴克也給出了具體解決方案。他提出「赫爾辛基協議2.0」（Helsinki Accord 2.0）的構想，主張西方國家應以維持市場開放為籌碼，要求北京當局保障中國人民的基本人權及宗教信仰自由，否則西方將逐步推動與中國經濟脫鉤。
他認為，此舉將在中國國內激起改革辯論並凝聚改革動力，而失去美國市場將對中共經濟造成毀滅性打擊，將有機會為中國人民帶來更大的自由。
布朗巴克最後表示，民主制度的優點，就是能夠承認過去的錯誤並予以糾正，「25年前，自由世界犯下了一個錯誤，如今是時候糾正了」。
他近期也出版了《中共對信仰的戰爭》（China’s War on Faith）一書，持續關注中國宗教迫害議題。
在中國加入世貿組織滿25周年之際，反思當年對華貿易政策的聲音在美國政界頻繁出現。
賓夕法尼亞州共和黨籍聯邦參議員戴夫‧麥考米克（Dave McCormick）於2026年10月在哈德遜研究所演說時也表示，華府兩黨25年前在對華政策上「賭錯了」，誤判了北京的動機與意圖。
美國財政部長斯科特‧貝森特（Scott Bessent）與貿易代表傑米森‧格里爾（Jamieson Greer）亦曾公開指出，當年允許中國入世是一項重大戰略失誤，導致美國製造業基礎被掏空。
大紀元系列社論《九評共產黨》曾對中共的政治本質做出了深刻的分析，社論在「評中國共產黨的流氓本性」中指出，「其許願的『改革』只是出於維護中共的統治，只能是換湯不換藥的跛足改革。」
社論引用了中共喉舌《人民日報》在2004年7月12日頭版中發表的文字，稱中共「決不能變，變則自我瓦解」，凸顯了中共維持現有政治體制與推動根本性政治改革之間的深層矛盾。
《九評》社論指出，「同共產黨談改良民主，無疑與虎謀皮」。
長期關注中國問題的海外評論人士也曾指出，中共政治體制與人權保障之間存在著根本性矛盾。2026年2月，由魏京生、王丹、王軍濤等海外民運人士召集的第二屆中國國是會議發布《經濟議題公報》指出，任何試圖在現有專制框架內「修修補補」的做法，都是飲鴆止渴。

content:
香港警方启用闭路电视AI人脸识别，人权组织忧虑监控扩大 · 茉莉花新闻网 在新标签页中打开
香港警方11月16日起在全港“锐眼计划”闭路电视监控网络中启用人工智能人脸识别功能。总部位于纽约的人权基金会（HRF）在新一期《人工智能与个人权利》通讯中指出，该系统的人脸识别数据将保存约180天，是一般闭路电视录像保存期限的6倍，可能被用于自动追踪当局视为不受欢迎人士的实际位置。
人权基金会表示，香港警方此前曾利用监控镜头监视争取民主的示威活动，并收集影像作为调查证据；此次扩大监控网络并加入人脸识别技术，可能进一步增强政治打压能力。
警务处处长周一鸣11月15日在电视节目中表示，该系统并非“想用就用”，使用人脸识别须经过审批并设有制约与平衡机制，主要针对罪案及失踪人口案件。他说，闭路电视已协助侦破包括谋杀、纵火在内的超过2000宗案件，拘捕近3000人，今年9月更录得“零劫案”。被问及系统能否识别戴口罩人士时，他以避免有心人掌握逃避侦查的方法为由，拒绝透露技术细节。
港府自2024年起分3阶段推进“锐眼计划”，截至今年11月初，警方自行安装及接入公营机构的镜头已超过1万个，目标是到2028年增至6万支。首批已有奥海城、屯门市广场、葵涌商场及房协粉岭“岭·乐活”4个商场同意接入系统。周一鸣说，接驳商场系统时需设立防火墙以防资料外泄或黑客入侵，镜头全部拍摄公众地方。
此外，警方还计划扩大无人机中央机库，把地面巡逻扩展为“天空巡逻”，大方向是设立200个无人机库，目前已在港岛区试行。
周一鸣以全部镜头只拍公众地方来回应滥用疑虑，但警方监控覆盖范围已在向外延伸。奥海城、屯门市广场等4个商场已同意把闭路电视接入警方系统，人权基金会所指人脸识别数据约180天的保存期也是一般录像的6倍；对于下一步是否推展至私人屋苑，警方给出的回答是先审视成效再作决定。

title: Joshua Wong’s prison letters reveal inner shift as Hong Kong activist faces another decade behind bars
